stories.title: API Discovery: Verify and Document Skyscanner RapidAPI Contract
stories.description: Before implementing the Skyscanner client, discover and document the real RapidAPI endpoint contract. Using the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable, make live curl probes (via the Bash tool only — FetchUrl and WebSearch are prohibited) against the subscribed Skyscanner host to identify: (1) the correct x-rapidapi-host value, (2) working endpoint paths for flight search (one-way and/or roundtrip), (3) required query parameters with exact names and value formats, and (4) the response JSON shape including top-level keys and nested field names relevant to FlightResult. Write the discovered contract to /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md. This file is the authoritative reference for SKY-002 (client implementation). Probe with `curl -si` so both status codes and response bodies are captured. A 429 (Too Many Requests) confirms a path is valid even when no 2xx body is obtained. Do NOT write any TypeScript, JavaScript, or compiled output in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: PREREQUISITE GATE: The RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable must be set and non-empty before any probe is executed. If it is absent or empty, the story must abort immediately with a clear error message ('RAPIDAPI_KEY is not set — aborting discovery') and no curl probes, directory creation, or file writes may occur. This gate must be verified as the very first step.

The probe sequence is executed in this exact order: (1) verify RAPIDAPI_KEY is non-empty (abort if not), (2) `mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs`, (3) two or more `curl -si` probes against candidate endpoints on skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com, (4) write api-contract.md with all required sections — no section may be written before the relevant probes have been run.

ABORT CONDITION: If every probed endpoint returns 404 (i.e. no endpoint returns 2xx or 429), the story must abort without writing api-contract.md, and instead write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/discovery-failure.md containing: the date, all probed URLs, all observed status codes, and the message 'No working endpoints found — SKY-001b cannot produce a valid contract. Human review required before SKY-002 proceeds.'

/tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/ directory exists and /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md is present and non-empty (this AC is only reachable if the prerequisite gate passed and at least one non-404 probe was obtained).
No TypeScript, JavaScript, compiled output, package.json, lockfiles, or any dependency manifest files are created or modified as part of this story.

technicalNotes.notes: CRITICAL: Use your Bash tool to run curl commands directly. Do NOT use FetchUrl, WebSearch, or any web browsing tool. Do NOT look up external documentation. Run curl -si probes immediately using the Bash tool. RAPIDAPI_KEY is available in the environment. Known candidate host: skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com (429 responses confirm subscription active). sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com returns 404 — do not use it. A 429 (Too Many Requests) on an endpoint confirms the path is valid — document it. The goal is an accurate contract doc, not a working implementation. Probe sequence: (1) mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs, (2) run 2-3 curl -si probes to candidate endpoints, (3) write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md with all required sections.

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client with unit tests
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI and write src/skyscanner/client.test.ts in the same story. The client must export SkyscannerClient, SearchParams, and FlightResult. It must use the global fetch exclusively, validate inputs, sanitize the API key, handle HTTP errors, malformed responses, pagination (header-based), and unexpected runtime errors. Tests must use vi.stubGlobal for fetch mocking with afterEach vi.unstubAllGlobals(). Both tsc --noEmit and vitest run must exit 0 before the story is marked complete.
acceptanceCriteria: src/skyscanner/client.ts exports a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor signature is exactly: constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported from client.ts with exactly these fields: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number — no additional required fields

FlightResult interface is exported from client.ts with exactly these fields: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number — no additional required fields
searchFlights uses the Node.js global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, got, or any other HTTP library is imported in client.ts
Every fetch call in searchFlights includes a 'User-Agent' header in the request headers object

When no apiKey is passed to the constructor and the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is unset or empty, constructing SkyscannerClient throws an Error whose message references the missing key (e.g. contains 'API key')
When apiKey is passed as an empty string ('') to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the same missing-key Error as when apiKey is omitted entirely
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string in the environment and no apiKey is provided to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the missing-key Error
When an apiKey is provided to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set in the environment, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence over the environment variable

The constructor sanitizes the resolved apiKey value using the regex /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ (allowing alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens); if the key does not match, the constructor throws an Error indicating an invalid API key format
The apiKey is stored as a private field (using the private keyword or # prefix) on the SkyscannerClient instance and is not publicly accessible

searchFlights validates the date parameter against the regex /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ inline (no separate isValidDate helper function); if the format is invalid, searchFlights throws a descriptive Error before making any network call
When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx HTTP status, searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message includes the numeric HTTP status code
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the apiKey value anywhere in its message string
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the full request URL in its message string (to prevent leaking query parameters or other sensitive data)

When the API response body is not a plain array (Array.isArray(data) === false) or is missing any of the seven required FlightResult fields (price, currency, airline, departure, arrival, duration, stops) on any element, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error

searchFlights checks the response header 'x-next-page' via res.headers?.get?.('x-next-page') to determine if pagination is needed; if the header is present and non-null, the client fetches subsequent pages and concatenates results before resolving

The pagination loop in searchFlights includes a termination guard (e.g., a maximum page count or a check that the next-page URL differs from the current URL) to prevent infinite loops if the server repeatedly returns the same next-page header value

Unexpected runtime errors caught in the catch block of searchFlights that are not already SkyscannerClient-originated errors are re-thrown wrapped in a new Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i

SkyscannerClient-originated errors (constructor validation errors, date validation errors, HTTP errors, parse errors) are NOT re-wrapped by the runtime error catch block — they propagate with their original message intact

When fetch itself rejects (e.g., network timeout, DNS failure — the Promise returned by fetch rejects rather than resolving with a non-ok response), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i

When adults is omitted from SearchParams, searchFlights constructs the fetch URL without an 'adults' query parameter (or uses a documented default value) — the behavior must be deterministic and not produce 'undefined' in the URL string
src/skyscanner/client.test.ts contains at least 6 vitest tests using vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) for mocking, with afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); }) — vi.spyOn is not used for fetch

Every vi.stubGlobal fetch mock in client.test.ts returns an object with all four fields: ok, status, json (async function), and headers: { get: () => null } — absence of headers will cause a TypeError on the pagination check
The fetch stub used in success-path tests returns a plain array (not a wrapped object) as the resolved value of json(), matching the Array.isArray check in the client
client.test.ts test (a): verifies the correct RapidAPI URL is constructed from SearchParams fields and that request headers include the API key and User-Agent
client.test.ts test (b): verifies a successful response body (plain array of FlightResult-shaped objects) is parsed and returned as FlightResult[]
client.test.ts test (c): verifies that a fetch response with ok=false and status=4xx causes searchFlights to reject with an Error whose message contains the status code
client.test.ts test (d): verifies that constructing SkyscannerClient with no apiKey and no RAPIDAPI_KEY env var throws an Error referencing the missing key
client.test.ts test (e): verifies that a fetch response whose json() resolves to a non-array or object missing required fields causes searchFlights to reject with a parse/validation Error
client.test.ts test (f): verifies that when the fetch stub rejects entirely (simulating a network-level failure), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i
Any test in client.test.ts that sets process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY must restore the original value (or delete the key) in afterEach or afterAll to prevent cross-test environment contamination
All SkyscannerClient instantiations in tests use the object constructor form: new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: 'valid_api_key' })

The test API key used in client.test.ts is a value matching /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ — specifically a value containing underscores or hyphens (e.g., 'valid_api_key') to exercise the correct sanitization regex
tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no type errors across all files in the project
vitest run exits 0 with all tests passing and no skipped tests

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results via `renderTable` imported from `./table`. Columns in fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1. All process-exit and stderr responsibilities — including the searchFlights rejection path — are owned exclusively by `src/cli.ts`; `src/skyscanner/client.ts` re-throws errors and does not call `process.exit` or write to stderr. Shebang and chmod+x are explicitly out of scope; invocation is `node dist/cli.js`. SKY-003 is a parent (governance) story only; all actionable work is delegated to canonical split children SKY-003a (implementation) and SKY-003a-test (unit tests).
acceptanceCriteria: SKY-003 is a parent story only; all implementation work is delegated to split child SKY-003a and all test work to split child SKY-003a-test. No other split children (e.g. SKY-003b, SKY-003a-1, SKY-003a-2, SKY-003a-test-1, SKY-003a-test-2) are owned by this story; any such duplicates require human confirmation before being marked canonical.
No new runtime dependencies beyond Node built-ins and packages already present in `package.json` from SKY-001/SKY-002 are introduced by either child.

Shebang line and chmod+x are explicitly out of scope for this story and both children; the compiled output is invoked as `node dist/cli.js ...` only. (Decision recorded: no shebang, no execute bit, Node invocation only.)

`tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits a module format compatible with `node dist/cli.js` invocation (CommonJS or ESM with `.mjs` extension consistently applied); after `tsc`, `node dist/cli.js` exits without a module-resolution or syntax error.

All process-exit and stderr responsibilities, including the searchFlights rejection path (caught Error → message written to stderr + `process.exit(1)`), are owned exclusively by `src/cli.ts` and are delegated to split child SKY-003a. `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002) MUST re-throw errors and MUST NOT call `process.exit` or write to `process.stderr`. No other module in the dependency chain owns these responsibilities.

stories.title: Build HTML dashboard at src/public/index.html
stories.description: Create src/public/index.html — a clean, self-contained single-file HTML dashboard (no build step, no npm, just HTML+CSS+vanilla JS). The dashboard must: (1) have a search form with fields: From (IATA code), To (IATA code), Date (date picker), Adults (number input, default 1, min 1); (2) on form submit, call GET /search?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin and render results; (3) display results in a styled table with columns: Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops; (4) include a 'Find Cheapest' button that calls GET /cheapest?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin using the current form field values, and highlights or separately labels the cheapest row; (5) show a loading indicator while requests are in-flight and display error messages when requests fail; (6) support dark mode via CSS custom properties and prefers-color-scheme; (7) be mobile-responsive via responsive CSS (flexbox/grid or media queries). The file must be entirely self-contained — no external CDN links, no imported scripts or stylesheets. NOTE: IATA 3-letter uppercase format validation is intentionally deferred to a future hardening story; From/To fields accept free-form text with whitespace-trimming as specified in the child stories.
acceptanceCriteria: src/public/index.html exists and is served by the Express app as a static file at the root path

The document declares <meta charset='utf-8'>, contains <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'>, has a <title> element, and the root <html> element carries a lang attribute (e.g. lang='en')

The four search fields are contained in a <form> element; each field has a corresponding <label> associated via matching for/id attributes: From (type=text, IATA placeholder), To (type=text, IATA placeholder), Date (type=date), Adults (type=number, default value 1, min 1)
The form's submit handler calls event.preventDefault(); pressing Enter within any field triggers the same search as clicking the submit button, and no full-page reload or URL navigation occurs

The From, To, and Date fields carry the native required attribute (or equivalent JS validation is applied before any fetch is issued); submitting with any of those fields empty does NOT issue a network request — a validation message (native browser or inline) is shown instead

Field values for From and To are trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace before being encoded into query parameters; an input containing only whitespace is treated as empty and triggers the same validation message as a blank field
Submitting the form issues GET /search?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin with field values encoded via URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent

The 'Find Cheapest' button issues GET /cheapest?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin, passing the same four parameter values currently present in the search form fields at the time of the click; the button is keyboard-operable (focusable and activatable via Enter/Space) and is not a plain <div> or <span>

The search submit button is disabled (disabled attribute set) while a /search request is in-flight; the 'Find Cheapest' button is disabled (disabled attribute set) while a /cheapest request is in-flight — preventing duplicate concurrent requests for each respective action; both buttons are re-enabled once their respective request resolves (success or error)

A loading indicator (spinner or 'Searching...' text) is visible while a /search request is in-flight and is hidden (display:none or equivalent) once the request resolves (success or error); a separate or shared loading indicator is visible while a /cheapest request is in-flight and hidden once it resolves

Loading indicators and error messages are placed in or associated with an aria-live='polite' region or role='alert' element so screen reader users are notified of state changes without requiring focus movement
On a successful /search response the results table renders one row per flight with columns: Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops

The results table uses <thead> containing <th scope='col'> elements for each column header (Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops) and a <tbody> for data rows, so screen readers can associate cells with headers

If /search returns an empty flights array (data.flights.length === 0), a 'No results found' (or equivalent) message is displayed and no stale rows or header-only empty table from a prior search remain visible
If /search returns an HTTP error or the fetch rejects (network failure), an error message is displayed inline in the UI (not just logged to console.log)
If /cheapest returns an HTTP error or the fetch rejects (network failure), an error message is displayed inline in the UI (not just logged to console.log)
A previously displayed error message is cleared when the next /search or /cheapest request begins, so stale error text does not persist alongside fresh results
Submitting a new search clears any previously rendered results table rows and any existing cheapest highlight before rendering the new response

The row in the results table matching the /cheapest response is visually distinguished (e.g. highlighted background or 'Cheapest' badge) and carries an accessible label (e.g. aria-label or a visually-hidden text node indicating it is the cheapest option); if no table results are currently displayed, the cheapest flight details (Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops) are shown in a separate clearly labelled summary section

All flight data from API responses is rendered using safe DOM methods (e.g. textContent, createElement, setAttribute) rather than by interpolating API-supplied strings directly into innerHTML — this prevents XSS if an upstream API field contains HTML or script content

When a second /search request is submitted while a prior /search request is still in-flight, the earlier request is aborted via AbortController and its response is discarded; when a second /cheapest request is submitted while a prior /cheapest request is still in-flight, the earlier request is aborted via AbortController — out-of-order responses must never overwrite results from a newer request

The page applies distinct background and foreground colors when the OS/browser prefers dark mode (via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) using CSS custom properties defined on :root); at minimum, background-color and color values differ meaningfully from light-mode values

On a viewport width of 375px the form fields and results table are usable without horizontal scrolling of the page body — the table either scrolls horizontally within its own container (overflow-x: auto on a wrapper) or its columns stack/reflow appropriately

The HTML file contains no <link rel='stylesheet' href='...'> pointing to external origins and no <script src='...'> pointing to external origins — all CSS is in a <style> block and all JS is in a <script> block within the single file

stories.title: CLI argument parsing, env-var guard, and SkyscannerClient wiring (cli.ts implementation only)
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` with manual `process.argv` flag parsing (no commander/yargs/minimist). Export `parseArguments`, `validateArguments`, and `main` with the exact signatures defined in AC-2. `validateArguments` MUST throw `new Error('exit:2')` or `new Error('exit:1')` — it must NOT call `process.exit` directly. `main()` catches those thrown errors and calls `process.exit(N)`; any non-exit error is re-thrown unchanged. Flag validation order: `--from`, `--to`, `--date`, `--adults`, then `RAPIDAPI_KEY`. Use `Number()` (not `parseInt()`) to parse `--adults`. Construct `SkyscannerClient` with an object arg `{ apiKey }`. Call `renderTable` conditionally: pass currency only when defined. Write all errors to `process.stderr.write()`, not `console.error()`. Guard module entry with `if (require.main === module) { main(); }`. Do NOT write `cli.test.ts` — that file is exclusively owned by SKY-003a-test. Network errors and non-2xx API responses are explicitly out of scope here; they are re-thrown by `main()` and handled in SKY-003b.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 FILE & IMPORTS: `src/cli.ts` exists and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors on the project; no third-party flag-parsing library (commander, yargs, minimist, or any equivalent) is imported anywhere in the file; `src/cli.ts` imports `SkyscannerClient` from `'./skyscanner/client'` (subdirectory path) and `renderTable` from `'./table'`; no subprocess utilities (`spawnSync`, `execSync`, `child_process`) appear anywhere in the file; `src/cli.test.ts` is NOT created by this story

AC-2 EXPORTED SIGNATURES & INTERFACES: `src/cli.ts` exports exactly these three symbols with these exact signatures: `export function parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments`, `export function validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments`, and `export async function main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>`; `ValidatedArguments` MUST include at minimum the fields `from: string`, `to: string`, `date: string`, `adults: number`, `rapidApiKey: string`, and `currency?: string` — the `currency` field MUST be typed as `string | undefined` so that AC-11's conditional renderTable call is type-safe; any deviation in export name, arity, or interface shape is a failure

AC-3 FLAG PARSING MECHANICS: flag values are read from the space-separated token immediately following each flag (e.g. `--from CDG` yields `from === 'CDG'`); parsing is order-independent (`--to LHR --from CDG --date 2025-09-01` produces the same result as `--from CDG --to LHR --date 2025-09-01`); a recognized flag with no following value token (last argv element, or immediately followed by another `--flag`) is treated as absent and routed through normal validation; unrecognized flags are silently ignored and do not alter exit codes

AC-4 VALIDATION ORDER & PRECEDENCE: validation follows this strict check order: `--from` presence, `--to` presence, `--date` presence and format, `--adults` validity, then `RAPIDAPI_KEY` presence; argument validation always completes before env-var validation; when multiple errors are present only the first failure in this order is reported; if both a required flag is missing AND `RAPIDAPI_KEY` is absent the process exits 2 (not 1) and the env-var error is never emitted

AC-5 THROW MECHANISM — NO DIRECT process.exit IN validateArguments: `validateArguments` MUST throw `new Error('exit:2')` for all argument-validation failures and `new Error('exit:1')` for a missing/empty `RAPIDAPI_KEY`; it must NOT call `process.exit()` directly at any point; `main()` catches errors whose `message` starts with `'exit:'`, extracts the numeric suffix via `err.message.split(':')[1]`, and calls `process.exit(Number(code))`; any error whose message does not start with `'exit:'` is re-thrown unchanged to the caller

AC-6 REQUIRED FLAGS — from, to, date: each of `--from`, `--to`, and `--date` is individually required; omitting any one causes `validateArguments` to throw `new Error('exit:2')` after writing a usage hint to `process.stderr.write()` that names the missing flag; `--date` value must additionally match `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/` and a non-matching value triggers the same throw with a descriptive message written to `process.stderr.write()`; stdout is empty in all these error cases

AC-7 OPTIONAL FLAG — adults: `--adults` is optional and defaults to `1` when absent; the value is parsed with `Number()` (NOT `parseInt()`); a value that is non-numeric, non-integer (detected via `!Number.isInteger(Number(value))`), zero, or negative causes `validateArguments` to throw `new Error('exit:2')` with a descriptive message written to `process.stderr.write()`; the parsed adults integer (including the implicit default of `1`) is forwarded verbatim to `searchFlights` and never silently coerced

stories.title: Server skeleton: /health, GET /, API-key middleware, error handling, and package.json scripts
stories.description:
Create the Express server skeleton in src/server.ts with the module-guard pattern, the /health and GET / routes, the RAPIDAPI_KEY absence middleware (503 short-circuit), the global error handler (500), and the package.json 'start'/'build' scripts. This slice has no runtime dependency on SKY-002 and can be implemented and merged in parallel with it. supertest and @types/supertest must be installed. A minimal test file (at least 5 tests) covering /health, GET /, 503 gating, global error handler, and module-guard must pass.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS (violations cause all tests to fail):
- src/server.ts MUST end with `export default app`; test file does `import app from './server'`.
- NEVER call app.listen() unconditionally; guard with `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test') { app.listen(3000); }`.
- Only use installed packages: express, @types/express. Do NOT import helmet, morgan, uuid, cors, or any uninstalled package.
- Do NOT use import.meta anywhere — this is a CommonJS (require.main) project.
- Do NOT add req.id or any custom property to Express Request without augmenting the type.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) AND a `export default app` so that `import app from './server'` in test files receives a valid Express application instance without binding a port
The `listen()` call in src/server.ts is guarded with `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test') { app.listen(...) }` so that `vitest run` never binds a port and supertest can import the module safely
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body matching `{ status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }` regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set or absent
GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type matching text/html and body equal to the contents of src/public/index.html
src/public/index.html exists, contains valid HTML with at minimum a non-empty `<html>` root element, and is served correctly by the GET / route

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialization, a single middleware registered at startup short-circuits all requests to GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body `{ error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }`; GET /health and GET / are unaffected by this middleware

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var IS present at server initialization, GET /search and GET /cheapest are NOT short-circuited by the API-key absence middleware (they may return 404 or be handled by downstream routes, but must not return 503 due to the absence middleware)

When a route handler or downstream middleware calls `next(err)` with an Error object, the global error handler returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body `{ error: <string> }` and does not crash the process or emit an unhandled promise rejection

When `next(err)` is called with a non-Error value (e.g. a plain string or object), the global error handler still returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body `{ error: <string> }` without throwing or crashing
The global error handler is registered after all route definitions in src/server.ts using the 4-arity signature `(err, req, res, next)` so Express correctly identifies it as an error handler

The global error handler does NOT expose raw stack traces or internal error details in the response body when NODE_ENV is 'production' — the `error` field contains only a safe, generic message string in that environment
package.json contains a 'start' script with value `node dist/server.js`
package.json contains a 'build' script that produces dist/server.js such that `npm run build && npm run start` starts the server and GET /health returns HTTP 200
supertest and @types/supertest are listed in package.json devDependencies and are importable in test files without TypeScript errors
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no type errors AND `vitest run` exits 0 with all tests passing (minimum 5 tests covering /health, GET /, 503 gating, global error handler, and module-guard isolation)

src/server.ts contains no import of helmet, morgan, uuid, cors, import.meta, or any package not listed in package.json dependencies/devDependencies; `npx tsc --noEmit` must confirm zero unresolved-module errors

1. EXPORT DEFAULT: server.ts must end with "export default app". server.test.ts does "import app from './server'" — if there is no default export, app is undefined and every supertest request throws.
2. NEVER call app.listen() unconditionally. Guard it: if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'test') { app.listen(3000); }
3. Import SkyscannerClient from './skyscanner/client' not './skyscanner-client'.

stories.description: Executable verification that the scaffolded project at /tmp/skyscanner-app passes TypeScript compilation and vitest run with no errors. Depends on SKY-001-A completing successfully.
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npx tsc --noEmit' exits with code 0 and produces no output on stdout and no output on stderr.
Running 'cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npx vitest run' exits with code 0; a 'No test files found' message on stdout is an acceptable outcome and is not treated as a failure.
package.json contains a 'test' script entry (for example "test": "vitest run") so that 'npm test' does not exit non-zero with a missing-script error.
package.json contains both a 'start' script equal to 'node dist/server.js' and a 'build' script equal to 'tsup', so that external verification can execute the produced artifact.

tsconfig.json does not set compilerOptions.module to 'CommonJS' in a way that blocks vitest from loading vitest.config.ts as ESM; an acceptable resolution is module set to ESNext, NodeNext, or Bundler, OR package.json contains "type": "module", OR vitest.config.ts uses an ESM-forcing extension such as .mts or .mjs.
Running 'node --check /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist/server.js' exits with code 0, which validates that the build output is syntactically valid JavaScript independent of the build script's exit code.

Running 'cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npm run build' exits with code 0 and the file /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist/server.js exists after the command completes, which is the artifact referenced by the start script.

Running 'rm -rf /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist && cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npm run build' exits with code 0, and after the command completes the file /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist/server.js exists and has an mtime greater than or equal to the mtime of /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist immediately before the build started, demonstrating a fresh build artifact with no reliance on pre-existing files in dist/.
Running 'cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npm test' exits with code 0, which proves the 'test' script is defined in package.json and is not missing.

Running 'cd /tmp/skyscanner-app && npx vitest run' does not emit the string 'Vitest cannot be imported in a CommonJS module' on stdout or stderr, confirming vitest.config.ts sets include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'].
The built artifact at /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist/server.js is executable and does not contain syntax errors that would cause Node.js to fail during runtime.
The build process does not generate any error or warning messages that indicate potential runtime issues in the compiled JavaScript.
The package.json file includes a 'build' script set to 'tsup' and a 'start' script that references 'node dist/server.js', ensuring the project can be built and started correctly.
The tsconfig.json file is correctly configured to allow TypeScript compilation to succeed without errors or warnings, including proper module resolution for ESM compatibility.
The vitest.config.ts file is present and includes the configuration necessary to run tests from source files in the src directory, specifically including ['src/**/*.test.ts'].
The project scaffolded at /tmp/skyscanner-app does not include any files that would cause the build process to fail due to forbidden extensions or invalid configurations.
The project's build process completes successfully and produces a valid JavaScript file at the expected location without any dependency resolution failures.
The build artifact at /tmp/skyscanner-app/dist/server.js is generated with the correct permissions that allow execution by the Node.js runtime.

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client (client.ts)
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI using the global fetch. Export SkyscannerClient class, SearchParams interface, and FlightResult interface. Implement input validation, API key sanitization, HTTP error handling, malformed-response detection, header-based pagination, User-Agent header, and runtime error wrapping. tsc --noEmit must exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: src/skyscanner/client.ts exports a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor signature is exactly: constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported with exactly: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number
FlightResult interface is exported with exactly: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number
searchFlights uses the Node.js global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, got, or any other HTTP library is imported
Every fetch call includes a 'User-Agent' header in the request headers object
When no apiKey is passed and RAPIDAPI_KEY is unset or empty, the constructor throws an Error whose message references the missing key
When apiKey is an empty string, the constructor throws the same missing-key Error
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string and no apiKey is provided, the constructor throws the missing-key Error
When apiKey is provided and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence
The constructor validates the resolved apiKey against /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/; if it does not match, the constructor throws an Error indicating invalid API key format
The apiKey is stored as a private field (private keyword or # prefix) and is not publicly accessible
searchFlights validates the date parameter inline against /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/; if invalid, throws a descriptive Error before any network call
When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the numeric HTTP status code but not the apiKey value
When the response body is not a plain array or is missing required fields, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error
searchFlights checks res.headers?.get?.('x-next-page') for pagination and fetches subsequent pages if the header is present and non-null
Unexpected runtime errors are caught and re-thrown wrapped in a new Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i
tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no type errors

stories.title: Vitest test suite for cli.ts (cli.test.ts)
stories.description: Write `src/cli.test.ts` that imports and tests the exported `parseArguments`, `validateArguments`, and `main` functions from `src/cli.ts`. Use `vi.hoisted()` before `vi.mock()` to set up mocks. Mock `./skyscanner/client` and `./table`. Spy on `process.stderr.write` to capture stderr output. Mock `process.exit` to throw `Error('process.exit:N')` so the Vitest process is not aborted. Do NOT use subprocesses (`spawnSync`, `execSync`, `child_process`). Do NOT use `require()` inside tests. This story owns only `src/cli.test.ts`; the implementation file `src/cli.ts` is owned by the sibling story SKY-003a-impl.
acceptanceCriteria: All Vitest tests in `src/cli.test.ts` pass with zero failures when `vitest run` is executed against the project.

`vi.hoisted()` is called before any `vi.mock()` call and its return value is destructured as `{ MockSkyscannerClient, mockSearchFlights, mockRenderTable }` where: `mockSearchFlights` is `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([{ flight: 'mock' }])`; `MockSkyscannerClient` is `vi.fn(function(this: any) { this.searchFlights = mockSearchFlights; })`; `mockRenderTable` is `vi.fn()`. A rejecting variant `mockSearchFlights.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('network failure'))` is used in the arrange step of the rejection-path test (case k) — the hoisted default remains the resolving mock for all other tests.

`vi.mock('./skyscanner/client', () => ({ SkyscannerClient: MockSkyscannerClient }))` and `vi.mock('./table', () => ({ renderTable: mockRenderTable }))` are declared at module scope immediately after the `vi.hoisted()` assignment — no other code appears between them.

A `beforeEach` block: (a) resets mocks by calling `MockSkyscannerClient.mockClear()`, `mockSearchFlights.mockClear()`, and `mockRenderTable.mockClear()` individually (`vi.clearAllMocks()` is NOT used anywhere in the file); (b) creates or resets `stderrSpy` via `vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write').mockImplementation(() => true)`; (c) mocks `process.exit` via `vi.spyOn(process, 'exit').mockImplementation((code) => { throw new Error('process.exit:' + code); })`.

Every error-path test (cases a–k) assembles captured stderr as `stderrSpy.mock.calls.flat().join('')`, asserts it is a non-empty string containing the expected text, AND asserts that `mockRenderTable` was never called (confirming stdout-equivalent output is empty).

The suite covers all of the following error-path cases, each in its own `it` block: (a) missing `--from` flag → `main` rejects with `'process.exit:2'`, stderr contains `'--from'`, `renderTable` not called, stderr non-empty; (b) missing `--to` flag → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr contains `'--to'`, `renderTable` not called, stderr non-empty; (c) missing `--date` flag → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr contains `'--date'`, `renderTable` not called, stderr non-empty; (d) invalid `--date` format (e.g. `'not-a-date'`) → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (e) `--adults` set to a non-numeric string → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (f) `--adults '1.5'` (float) → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (g) `--adults '0'` (zero) → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (h) `--adults '-1'` (negative) → rejects `'process.exit:2'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (i) absent `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var → rejects `'process.exit:1'`, stderr contains exact text `'Error: RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is required'`, `renderTable` not called, stderr non-empty; (j) empty-string `RAPIDAPI_KEY` → rejects `'process.exit:1'`, stderr non-empty, `renderTable` not called; (k) `searchFlights` rejects with `new Error('network failure')` — arranged via `mockSearchFlights.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('network failure'))` in the test's arrange step before calling `main` — `main` must reject or throw with `'process.exit:1'`, stderr contains `'network failure'` (or equivalent error message text), `renderTable` not called, stderr non-empty.

The suite covers all of the following happy-path cases, each in its own `it` block, with `RAPIDAPI_KEY` set to a non-empty string in the `env` argument passed to `main` (tests do NOT rely on real `process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY`): (a) omitting `--adults` causes `searchFlights` to be called with `adults: 1` (default value); (b) providing all valid flags (`--from LHR --to JFK --date 2025-09-01 --adults 2`) causes `searchFlights` to be called exactly once with `{ origin: 'LHR', destination: 'JFK', date: '2025-09-01', adults: 2 }` and `renderTable` to be called exactly once with the array returned by `mockSearchFlights`.

No subprocess utilities (`spawnSync`, `execSync`, `child_process`) are imported or referenced anywhere in `cli.test.ts`; all test cases invoke `parseArguments`, `validateArguments`, and `main` as directly imported ES module functions. `require()` is not used inside `cli.test.ts`; all imports are ES module `import` statements or `vi.hoisted`/`vi.mock` calls. Running `tsc --noEmit` on the project reports zero TypeScript errors after `cli.test.ts` is present.

technicalNotes.notes: This story is already a split child (splitDepth=2). No further splitting. The rejection-path test (case k) requires mockSearchFlights.mockRejectedValueOnce in the arrange step of that specific test; the hoisted default mockResolvedValue remains for all other tests. CRITICAL: cli.ts must use process.stderr.write, not console.error, or all stderr assertions will return empty string. CRITICAL: validateArguments must throw Error('exit:N'), not call process.exit directly; main() catches and converts to process.exit(N).

stories.title: Automated gate checks: Skyscanner mini-app review
stories.description: Execute the eleven automated gate checks (GATE-TS, GATE-TEST-EXIT, GATE-TEST-RESULTS, GATE-TEST-COVERAGE, GATE-SECRET, GATE-INPUT-400, GATE-ERROR-HANDLING, GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR, GATE-PATH-SAFETY, GATE-CONTENT-TYPE, GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT, GATE-CORS) against /tmp/skyscanner-app and verify that each exits clean. The review-agent records results in /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md and sets the Verdict token to PASS only when every sub-check passes. Depends on SKY-006-a producing the review scaffold and on SKY-001–SKY-005 delivering a complete implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: GATE-TS: Running `tsc --noEmit` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0 and produces zero lines of diagnostic output on both stdout and stderr. tsconfig.json at the project root must contain `"strict": true` under `compilerOptions`. If the root tsconfig.json uses an `extends` field (directly or transitively), no file in that extends chain may set `"strict": false` or override any strict sub-flag (e.g. `noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`) to `false`. The gate check must capture both stdout and stderr separately and record both in the review document; a non-empty stderr alone (even with exit code 0) is treated as a gate WARNING that must be explicitly noted.

GATE-TEST-EXIT + GATE-TEST-RESULTS: Running `npx vitest run` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0 (any non-zero exit code is a gate failure). The vitest output reports 0 failed tests, 0 skipped tests, and 0 todo tests; at least 1 test must be reported as passed to prevent an empty suite from producing a false PASS. Tests inside `describe.skip`, `it.skip`, `test.skip`, or `test.todo` blocks count as skipped/incomplete and cause this gate to fail. No line/branch coverage floor is imposed by this story — a separate coverage-floor story should be opened if a floor is desired.

GATE-TEST-COVERAGE: At least one non-empty test file (*.test.ts or *.spec.ts) exists under each of the three implementation layers — client (e.g. src/client/ or equivalent), CLI (e.g. src/cli/ or equivalent), and server/routes (e.g. src/server/, src/routes/, or equivalent). Each such file must (a) be syntactically valid TypeScript, (b) contain at least one `it()` or `test()` call that is not inside a `.skip` block, and (c) not consist solely of type-import statements with no runtime assertions. Each test file is counted under exactly one layer (no double-counting). The layer directory examples are illustrative; any directory whose name or path unambiguously maps to one of the three concerns satisfies the criterion.

GATE-SECRET: A case-insensitive grep for the literal Skyscanner API key value across all files under src/, test/, dist/, build/, .next/, out/, any *.env* files (excluding *.env.example and *.env.template), any captured test-output artefacts, and package-lock.json / yarn.lock returns zero matches. The key must be sourced exclusively from a named environment variable (e.g. SKYSCANNER_API_KEY) at runtime. Additionally, .gitignore (or equivalent VCS ignore file) must contain an entry that excludes all *.env files that may carry secrets (excluding *.env.example and *.env.template) — absence of .gitignore or a missing exclusion entry is a gate failure. If a CI pipeline artefact store is present, the CI pipeline must mask the environment variable value in all log output, verified by the absence of the key literal in any stored CI log artefact; if no CI pipeline is configured for this project, this sub-check is marked N/A-PASS and that determination is documented in the review.

GATE-INPUT-400: Every Express route that declares a required parameter (path, query, or body) returns HTTP 400 with (a) the header `Content-Type: application/json` and (b) a JSON body matching `{ "error": string }` when the parameter is (i) absent, (ii) present but empty string, and (iii) present but of an invalid type. Each of these three sub-cases must be covered by at least one automated test in the test suite.

GATE-ERROR-HANDLING + GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR: Every outbound API call is enclosed in a try/catch (or equivalent .catch()) block. Non-2xx responses from upstream are surfaced as a JSON body `{ "error": string, "status": number }` with a matching HTTP status code; the original upstream 4xx–5xx status code must be preserved; if the upstream returns a status outside 400–599 (e.g. 1xx, 3xx without redirect-following, or a network-level error including connection timeout, DNS failure, or ECONNREFUSED) the server must respond with HTTP 502. Every async Express route handler must either (a) be wrapped in a try/catch that calls `next(err)` on failure, or (b) be wrapped by a utility (e.g. `asyncHandler`) that forwards thrown errors to Express's error-handling middleware — no async route handler may allow an unhandled promise rejection to propagate silently. At least one automated test must verify that an async route that throws internally returns a structured error response rather than hanging or crashing. At least one automated test must verify that a simulated network-level error (e.g. fetch rejection) produces an HTTP 502 response with the correct JSON body.

GATE-PATH-SAFETY: If the Express app performs manual static-file serving (i.e. any route reads from the filesystem in response to a user-supplied path, beyond what `express.static` provides internally): user-supplied path segments must be sanitised using `path.resolve` (to eliminate `../` sequences) and `fs.realpath` or equivalent (to dereference symlinks), and validated to confirm the fully-resolved real path starts with the hard-coded base directory constant before any file I/O is performed. A test must demonstrate that a `../` traversal attempt returns HTTP 400 or 403 without reading outside the base directory, and a second test must demonstrate that a symlink pointing outside the base directory is also rejected. If the app uses only `express.static` for all static-file serving and performs no additional manual filesystem reads on user-supplied paths, the symlink-resolution sub-check is marked N/A-PASS and only the `express.static` usage must be confirmed in the review document.

GATE-CONTENT-TYPE: Every Express route that returns a JSON response (including error responses) sets the `Content-Type` header to `application/json` or `application/json; charset=utf-8`. This is verified by at least one automated test per route group that asserts on the response Content-Type header value. If CORS is active (see GATE-CORS), the OPTIONS preflight response must also set appropriate `Content-Type` (or omit a body entirely — an empty-body 204 is acceptable); a preflight response that returns a non-JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json` is a gate failure.

GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT: Running `npm audit --audit-level=high` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0, indicating zero high-severity or critical-severity vulnerabilities in the dependency tree. Any audit failure is treated as a gate failure and its full output is quoted verbatim in the review document.

GATE-CORS: The Express app's CORS policy is reviewed for correctness. Specifically: (a) if the app sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, this is flagged unless the app is explicitly documented as a public read-only API; (b) if the app uses the `cors` package or sets CORS headers manually, the allowed-origin list must be explicitly enumerated or derived from a validated environment variable — wildcard origins combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` must be treated as a gate failure; (c) at least one automated test asserts on the CORS headers returned by a representative route for a standard GET/POST request; (d) if CORS is active, at least one automated test must send an OPTIONS preflight request and assert that the response includes the correct `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` values. If the app serves no cross-origin clients and sets no CORS headers, this gate is marked N/A-PASS and that determination is documented in the review.

GATE-ENV-CONFIG: The application must validate all required environment variables at startup (before binding to a port or executing any business logic). If a required variable (e.g. SKYSCANNER_API_KEY) is absent or empty, the process must exit with a non-zero exit code and emit a human-readable error message to stderr identifying the missing variable by name. The application must NOT start successfully with a missing required environment variable and silently use an undefined/null value. At least one automated test (using environment-variable stubbing or process isolation) must verify that the application exits or throws on startup when a required variable is absent.

VERDICT: The review file /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md must contain exactly one line of the form `Verdict: <TOKEN>` where `<TOKEN>` matches the regular expression `^(PASS|FAIL)$` exactly (no trailing whitespace, no extra characters, no duplicate Verdict lines — a file containing two or more `Verdict:` lines is itself a gate failure). The token is `PASS` if and only if all gates enumerated in the ARTEFACT AC pass (including any N/A-PASS gates); it is `FAIL` followed on subsequent lines by a Markdown bullet list of the identifiers of every failing gate otherwise.

ARTEFACT: /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md must exist and be non-empty. It must contain one clearly labelled Markdown section per gate, using the gate identifier as the heading (## GATE-TS, ## GATE-TEST-EXIT + GATE-TEST-RESULTS, ## GATE-TEST-COVERAGE, ## GATE-SECRET, ## GATE-INPUT-400, ## GATE-ERROR-HANDLING + GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR, ## GATE-PATH-SAFETY, ## GATE-CONTENT-TYPE, ## GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT, ## GATE-CORS, ## GATE-ENV-CONFIG — eleven sections total). Each section must record: (1) the exact command invoked (if applicable), (2) the command's exit code, (3) observed command output or evidence quoted verbatim in a fenced code block, and (4) the pass/fail/N/A-PASS status. The file's last-modified filesystem timestamp must be equal to or later than the timestamp of the most recent gate-check run, preventing a stale cached artefact from being used. VCS commit of this file is explicitly out of scope for this story.

stories.description: Isolates the dependency-checking step from the substantive code review. This story succeeds when the /tmp/skyscanner-app workspace is confirmed to be in a reviewable state (src/ tree present, package.json present, tsconfig.json present, all five prior stories marked complete in the tracker). On success it emits a machine-readable gate-passed signal that SKY-006-B depends on. On failure it emits a BLOCKED signal and halts the pipeline without creating a partial review document.
acceptanceCriteria: Before any other action, the agent verifies the existence of all four required paths in order: /tmp/skyscanner-app (directory), /tmp/skyscanner-app/src (directory), /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json (file), and /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json (file). Checks are performed sequentially and stop at the first missing path.

If the /tmp/skyscanner-app/review directory does not exist, the agent creates it (including any intermediate directories) before writing any output files, regardless of whether the gate passes or fails.

If any required path is absent, the agent writes exactly one line to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md in the format `BLOCKED: dependency <missing-path> not satisfied` (where <missing-path> is the first failing path), writes the identical message to stderr, and exits with code 1. No additional content is appended to the review document.

If all required paths are present, the agent writes a JSON file at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json containing exactly the keys `story` (string, value `"SKY-006-A"`), `timestamp` (string, ISO-8601 UTC format), and `status` (string, value `"passed"`), then exits with code 0. No other keys are written to this file.

The gate check is idempotent: executing it multiple times against a fully valid workspace always exits with code 0 and overwrites /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json with an updated timestamp on each run, without duplicating or appending content.

The agent does not write any content to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md when the gate passes; that file is reserved exclusively for failure output and subsequent review content written by SKY-006-B.

All filesystem errors (e.g. permission denied when creating the review directory or writing output files) are caught, reported to stderr with a descriptive message prefixed `ERROR:`, and cause the agent to exit with code 2 to distinguish infrastructure failures from dependency failures.
The agent produces no stdout output under any execution path; all human-readable messaging is directed exclusively to stderr.

stories.title: Execute and document Skyscanner mini-app code review
stories.description: Performs the substantive five-category code review (TypeScript, Tests, Security, Error Handling, Express Safety) against the Skyscanner mini-app source and produces the final review document at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md. Execution is gated on SKY-006-A having written /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json with status 'passed'. This story owns all tool invocations, finding recording, Verdict determination, and exit-code signalling for CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Before executing any review step the agent reads /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json; if the file is absent or unreadable the agent halts immediately, emits a dependency error message to stderr that identifies the missing gate file by its full path, and exits with code 2; if the file is present and readable but is not valid JSON the agent exits with code 2 and emits a parse-error message to stderr that includes the file path and the JSON parse error description; if the file is valid JSON but does not contain the key-value pair '"status": "passed"' the agent exits with code 2 and emits a message identifying the file path and the actual value found; exit code 2 is distinct from exit code 1 (FAIL verdict) and exit code 0 (PASS verdict).

The agent performs a TypeScript category review: it inspects all .ts source files for strict-mode compliance, absence of untyped 'any' escape-hatches, correct interface/type usage, and absence of compiler errors reported by tsc --noEmit; every finding is recorded as a structured entry containing: file path (relative to /tmp/skyscanner-app), line number (a positive integer ≥ 1), severity (ERROR | WARN | INFO), gate name (e.g. TS_STRICT, TS_NO_ANY, TS_COMPILER_ERROR), and a one-sentence rationale; if a source file cannot be read due to permissions or I/O error the agent records a single ERROR-severity finding with gate name TS_FILE_UNREADABLE for that file and continues reviewing remaining files; if a source file matches the *.ts glob but is not valid UTF-8 text (e.g. a binary file with a .ts extension) the agent records a single WARN-severity finding with gate name TS_FILE_ENCODING_INVALID for that file, skips static analysis of that file, and continues processing remaining files — the finding must appear in the TypeScript Review section and the file must not be listed as analysed.

The agent performs a Tests category review: it verifies that a test suite exists and is executable, and that line-coverage meets or exceeds the target floor — the floor is the value declared in the project README or package.json (e.g. jest coverageThreshold.global.lines); if the project declares a branch or statement threshold instead of a line threshold, that declared metric and value is used as the floor; if no target is declared the default floor is 80% line coverage (NOTE: this default requires human policy confirmation); it also verifies that test files follow the project's naming and co-location conventions; every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2, using gate names such as TEST_SUITE_EXISTS, TEST_COVERAGE_FLOOR, TEST_NAMING_CONVENTION.

The agent performs a Security category review: it checks for hard-coded secrets or credentials (gate SECURITY_NO_HARDCODED_SECRETS), unsafe use of eval or the Function constructor (gate SECURITY_NO_EVAL), dependency versions with known CVEs using available lock-file data (gate SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CVE), and missing input sanitisation on user-supplied data (gate SECURITY_INPUT_SANITISATION); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The agent performs an Error Handling category review: it verifies that all async operations have explicit catch paths or are wrapped in try/catch (gate EH_ASYNC_CATCH), that error responses never leak stack traces or internal paths to HTTP clients (gate EH_NO_STACK_LEAK), that unhandled-rejection and uncaughtException process-level handlers are present (gate EH_PROCESS_HANDLERS), and that async Express route handlers do not throw without forwarding the error via next(err) (gate EH_EXPRESS_NEXT_ERR — a handler is non-compliant if it contains an await expression or returns a Promise and does not wrap its body in try/catch with a next(err) call in the catch block); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The agent performs an Express Safety category review: it checks for helmet or equivalent security-header middleware (gate EXPRESS_HELMET), rate-limiting middleware on public endpoints (gate EXPRESS_RATE_LIMIT), absence of directory-traversal vectors in static-file serving or path construction (gate EXPRESS_NO_PATH_TRAVERSAL), and CORS configuration (gate EXPRESS_CORS — PASS when cors() is called with an explicit origin allowlist or when CORS is intentionally disabled and a comment documents the rationale; FAIL when cors() is called with origin: '*' on a non-public API, when no CORS middleware is present on routes that accept cross-origin requests, or when the origin value is derived from an unsanitised request header); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The review document written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md contains exactly eight top-level sections in this order: (1) ## Executive Summary, (2) ## Scope & Methodology, (3) ## TypeScript Review, (4) ## Tests Review, (5) ## Security Review, (6) ## Error Handling Review, (7) ## Express Safety Review, (8) ## Verdict — each section heading formatted as a level-2 Markdown heading (## ); each of the five category review sections (TypeScript Review, Tests Review, Security Review, Error Handling Review, Express Safety Review) must contain at least one finding entry — either a genuine finding or an explicit INFO-severity 'no issues found' entry using the gate name <CATEGORY>_NO_ISSUES (e.g. TS_NO_ISSUES) — so that no section body is empty; a section that contains only a heading with no finding entries is treated as a placeholder and fails the no-placeholder check in AC-11.

The Verdict section must have ^(PASS|FAIL)$ as its first non-blank line (the token alone, no other text on that line); subsequent lines provide a concise rationale; Verdict is PASS only when zero ERROR-severity findings exist across all five categories, otherwise Verdict is FAIL.

The Executive Summary section includes: total finding counts broken down by category and by severity (ERROR / WARN / INFO), the overall Verdict token (PASS or FAIL), and the UTC timestamp at which the review completed in ISO-8601 format (e.g. 2024-06-01T12:34:56Z) with second-level precision and explicit 'Z' suffix.

The agent exits with code 0 when Verdict is PASS and with code 1 when Verdict is FAIL, allowing CI pipelines to gate on the exit code without parsing the document; exit code 2 is reserved exclusively for the gate-prerequisite failure described in AC-1; if the review document cannot be written to disk (e.g. directory does not exist, insufficient permissions, disk full) the agent emits an I/O error message to stderr identifying the target path and the OS error description, and exits with code 3 (distinct from codes 0, 1, and 2); the agent must not write any data to stdout or stderr that reveals the contents of environment variables, internal file paths outside /tmp/skyscanner-app, or process credentials — all diagnostic messages emitted to stderr are limited to: the gate-file error (AC-1), the I/O error described in this AC, and per-category progress indicators that contain only the category name and file count.

The review document is valid UTF-8 Markdown, contains no placeholder text (i.e. the literal strings 'TODO', 'TBD', 'FIXME', or 'N/A' used as a substitute for genuine analysis, or any section body that consists solely of whitespace), and every finding count stated in the Executive Summary is traceable to a corresponding named finding entry (identified by gate name, file path, and line number) in its respective category section; each finding entry must have a composite identifier (gate name + file path + line number) that is unique within the document — duplicate entries for the same location and gate are not permitted.

The document write operation is atomic from the reader's perspective: the agent writes the complete review content to a temporary file in the same directory (e.g. SKY-006-review.md.tmp) and renames it to the final path only after the write is fully flushed; if a previous run's output file already exists at the final path it is overwritten by the rename without leaving a partially written file.

stories.title: Code review (Part A): Prerequisites, document structure, TypeScript, and test checks
stories.description: First half of the Skyscanner mini-app code review. The agent verifies that all prerequisite stories are satisfied, creates the review document with the correct six-section structure, runs the TypeScript compiler, and verifies test execution and per-layer test coverage. Output is written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md. This story must be completed before SKY-006-B begins.
acceptanceCriteria: PREREQUISITE GATE — Before any review step executes the agent MUST verify: (a) the directory /tmp/skyscanner-app exists, (b) a src/ subtree is present beneath it containing at least one TypeScript source file (*.ts or *.tsx), and (c) a package.json is present at /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json. If any of these three conditions is not met the agent MUST immediately write a single-line file at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md containing exactly `BLOCKED: dependency SKY-00N not satisfied` (where N identifies the first unsatisfied story by its numeric suffix), emit the same message to stderr, exit with a non-zero code, and produce NO further review content. Any partial review document written after a failed prerequisite check is itself treated as a review failure.

The file /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md MUST be created (parent directory /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/ created if absent) and MUST contain all six required sections with exact H2 headings in this order and no other H2 headings: `## TypeScript`, `## Tests`, `## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`, `## Verdict`. Any missing heading, any heading with different casing or punctuation (e.g. `## Typescript` or `## TypeScript:` are both non-conforming), or any additional H2 heading anywhere in the document is a blocking structural finding that forces Verdict: FAIL.

A 'blocking finding' is defined as any discrete defect, failed check, or policy violation discovered during live inspection that, if left unresolved, would prevent the mini-app from meeting its stated requirements. Each blocking finding MUST be recorded as a numbered list item under the relevant category section and MUST include all four of the following fields: (1) the relative file path (relative to /tmp/skyscanner-app), (2) the line number or line range where the issue was observed, (3) a one-sentence description of the defect, and (4) the specific acceptance criterion or policy it violates. A finding that omits any of these four fields is itself considered incomplete, and the category containing it is treated as having an unresolved blocking finding.

Each of the five category sections (TypeScript, Tests, Security, Error Handling, Express Safety) MUST reference at least one concrete relative file path or specific line-number finding discovered during live inspection of the actual codebase at /tmp/skyscanner-app. Content that could have been produced without reading the actual source files (boilerplate, placeholder sentences, generic advice) constitutes a blocking structural finding for that section. For every finding the agent MUST record the exact tool invocation used to produce it (command run, exit code, and output truncated to 500 characters if longer) as a fenced code block immediately following the finding list item.

TypeScript check: The agent MUST run `tsc --noEmit --project /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json` and capture stdout, stderr, and exit code. Before running, the agent MUST read /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json and confirm that `"strict": true` appears in the top-level `compilerOptions` object of that file (not solely inherited via an `extends` chain without being re-stated); if it is absent, that absence is itself a blocking TypeScript finding recorded before the compiler is invoked. The tsc command MUST exit with code 0 and produce zero bytes on both stdout and stderr; any non-zero exit code or any diagnostic line on either stream is a blocking TypeScript finding. The raw command output (or a truncation to 2000 characters with a truncation notice) MUST be reproduced verbatim in the `## TypeScript` section.

Tests check — execution: The agent MUST read /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json, extract the value of `scripts.test`, and run that exact command from the /tmp/skyscanner-app working directory (falling back to `npx vitest run` only if the `test` key is absent or empty). The agent MUST capture stdout, stderr, and exit code. The command MUST exit with code 0. The Vitest (or equivalent runner) summary line MUST report 0 failed, 0 skipped, and 0 todo tests. Any non-zero exit code or any non-zero value in failed/skipped/todo counts is a blocking Tests finding. The raw summary output (last 2000 characters of combined stdout+stderr, with a truncation notice if trimmed) MUST be reproduced verbatim in the `## Tests` section.

Tests check — coverage by layer: At least one non-empty test file (containing at least one `it(`, `test(`, or `describe(` call) MUST be present for each of the following three layers: (a) Skyscanner API client — a file matching the glob `src/**/*.client.test.*` OR any file under src/ whose base name (without extension) contains both a word identifying the Skyscanner client module (e.g. 'client', 'skyscanner', 'api') and either 'test' or 'spec'; (b) CLI entry-point — any file under src/ whose base name contains a word identifying the CLI or bin module (e.g. 'cli', 'bin', 'index') and either 'test' or 'spec'; (c) Express server/router — any file under src/ whose base name contains a word identifying the server or router module (e.g. 'server', 'router', 'app') and either 'test' or 'spec'. Absence of a qualifying non-empty file for any single layer is a blocking Tests finding. The agent MUST list the resolved absolute path of each qualifying test file found in the `## Tests` section.

Upon completing all checks assigned to this story the agent MUST leave the review document in a consistent intermediate state: the `## TypeScript` and `## Tests` sections MUST be fully populated with findings and verbatim tool output as specified above; the remaining four sections (`## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`, `## Verdict`) MUST be present as H2 headings with no content beneath them (not even a blank placeholder line containing text). The document MUST NOT contain any line beginning with `Verdict:` or any text beneath the `## Verdict` heading until SKY-006-B writes it. Writing a Verdict line or populating the Security, Error Handling, or Express Safety sections in SKY-006-A is itself a blocking structural finding.

stories.title: Code review (Part B): Security, error handling, Express safety, and verdict
stories.description: Second half of the Skyscanner mini-app code review. The agent reads the partially-populated review document produced by SKY-006-A and performs deep inspection of security (API key exposure and query-parameter validation), error handling (missing-param 400 responses and upstream error propagation), and Express static-file safety (path traversal prevention). It then writes the `## Verdict` section and finalises the document. This story depends on SKY-006-A being complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Dependency-guard precondition: Before performing any category check, the agent MUST verify that `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` exists and contains ALL of the following H2 headings produced by SKY-006-A: `## TypeScript`, `## Tests`, `## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`. These heading names are the authoritative list inlined here — no cross-story AC reference is required. If the file is absent, empty, or missing any of these headings, the agent MUST abort with a non-zero exit code and emit a human-readable error message identifying the missing prerequisite; it MUST NOT create a partial or blank review document in this failure mode.

Security check — API key exposure: The agent MUST determine the exact string value assigned to the API key (from environment variable, config constant, or .env file under /tmp/skyscanner-app) and perform a case-insensitive literal grep for that value across: (a) all files under src/, (b) the captured stdout/stderr from the `vitest run` execution, and (c) any .log files under /tmp/skyscanner-app. Zero matches MUST be found across all three scopes; any match is a blocking Security finding. If the API key value cannot be determined (e.g. it is only read from process.env at runtime with no default), the agent MUST record this as an informational note and instead grep for the environment variable name to confirm it is never interpolated into a response body or log statement.

Security check — query parameter validation and binary file handling: Every Express route handler that accepts query parameters MUST validate each parameter before use via an explicit check (e.g. `if (!req.query.x)` or equivalent), a validation library schema (e.g. Zod, Joi, express-validator), or dedicated middleware — implicit type coercion alone is insufficient. The agent MUST enumerate all route handlers found in src/ and confirm each one validates its inputs; any route handler that uses a query parameter without prior explicit validation is a blocking Security finding. Additionally, if any route handler reads or serves files from disk, the agent MUST confirm that binary or non-UTF-8 file content is never decoded as UTF-8 text and re-emitted in an error message (which could expose partial binary data); any such path is a blocking Security finding.

Supply-chain secrets check: The agent MUST inspect the resolved contents of `node_modules/` (or, if node_modules is absent, the lockfile at `/tmp/skyscanner-app/package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`) for any file whose name matches `*.env`, `.env*`, `config.json`, or `secrets.*` at depth ≤ 2 within any single package directory. Each such file MUST be scanned for the API key value (if known) and for common credential patterns (bare 32+-character hex strings, strings matching `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, or strings matching `Bearer [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`). Any match is a blocking Security finding labelled `Supply-Chain Credential Exposure`. If node_modules is absent and no lockfile exists, the agent MUST record this as an informational note and skip this check without issuing a finding.

Error Handling check — missing/invalid parameters and Content-Type enforcement: Every Express route handler that declares a required query parameter MUST return HTTP 400 with a JSON body of the shape `{ "error": "<non-empty string>" }` (additional fields are permitted) when that parameter is: (a) absent from the request, (b) present but an empty string, or (c) present but not parseable as its declared type (e.g. a non-numeric string where a number is required). The agent MUST verify this by static analysis and, where the test suite exercises these paths, by inspecting the relevant test assertions. Failure of any sub-case (a), (b), or (c) for any route is a blocking Error Handling finding. Additionally, every error response (HTTP 4xx or 5xx) with a JSON body MUST set `Content-Type: application/json` — either via `res.json(...)` (which sets it automatically in Express) or via an explicit `res.setHeader`/`res.type('json')` call before `res.send(...)`; any error response path that sends a JSON-shaped body without an explicit or implicit `application/json` Content-Type is a blocking Error Handling finding.

Error Handling check — upstream error propagation (GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR): All code paths that invoke or await the upstream Skyscanner API MUST be wrapped in try/catch or .catch() / Promise rejection handling. Non-2xx HTTP status codes returned by the upstream MUST be mapped to a JSON response of the shape `{ "error": string, "status": number }` forwarded to the Express caller with the same HTTP status code or a semantically equivalent one (e.g. 502 Bad Gateway is acceptable for a 500 upstream). No unhandled-rejection or uncaught-exception path reachable via upstream errors is permitted. The agent MUST trace every call site to the upstream API in src/ and confirm coverage; any unguarded call site or missing non-2xx mapping is a blocking Error Handling finding. Express async error handlers MUST call `next(err)` rather than swallowing the error silently (GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR).

Express Safety check — path traversal prevention and CORS: Static file serving MUST use `express.static` with a base directory derived exclusively from a fixed, hard-coded constant (e.g. `path.join(__dirname, 'public')` or `path.resolve(__dirname, '../public')`). No user-controlled input MAY be concatenated, interpolated, or passed as an argument into `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, `path.resolve()`, `path.join()`, `fs.readFile()`, or any other file-system call used to derive the path of a served or read file. The agent MUST grep src/ for all occurrences of: `path.join`, `path.resolve`, `readFile`, `createReadStream`, and `sendFile`, and inspect each call site; any call site that incorporates user-controlled input is a blocking Express Safety finding. Additionally (EXPRESS_CORS gate): if a CORS middleware is present, the agent MUST confirm its `origin` option is not set to `'*'` in a production configuration; a wildcard CORS origin in a non-test context is a blocking Express Safety finding.

Verdict integrity: The `## Verdict` section MUST contain exactly one line matching the POSIX ERE regex `^(PASS|FAIL)$` (case-sensitive, anchored at both start and end of line, no leading or trailing whitespace, no punctuation, no markdown formatting) as the first non-blank line of that section. If the Verdict is FAIL, a prioritised numbered list of ALL blocking findings across all categories MUST follow immediately under the heading — with no intervening blank line or sub-heading — with each item cross-referencing its category name and the AC number it violates. The Verdict MUST be PASS if and only if all category checks produced zero blocking findings. A PASS verdict with any recorded blocking finding, or a FAIL verdict with no recorded blocking findings, is itself a review failure and the document MUST be regenerated from the point of the Verdict section.

Tool exit code authority: Before writing the Verdict line, the agent MUST collate all tool invocations across both SKY-006-A and SKY-006-B and record any that exited with a non-zero code. If any such non-zero exit code exists, the Verdict MUST be FAIL regardless of the narrative content of the category sections. The collated list of non-zero exit codes and the commands that produced them MUST appear as an appended sub-list under the first FAIL finding (or as a standalone finding if no other blocking findings were recorded), labelled `Tool Exit Code Failures`.

Document finalisation and atomic write: Upon writing the Verdict line the agent MUST perform a self-check verifying: (i) the final document contains exactly eight H2 headings in this exact order and with these exact names — `## TypeScript`, `## Tests`, `## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`, `## Verdict` (the first five from SKY-006-A plus `## Verdict` from this story, plus any two additional headings contributed by SKY-006-A as declared in its own AC-2 — the total MUST be eight; if SKY-006-A AC-2 declares fewer than eight, this check uses the count declared there), with no extra headings; and (ii) every blocking finding recorded in any section is represented in the Verdict's consolidated numbered list (if Verdict is FAIL). A document that passes this self-check MUST be written atomically — first to a uniquely-named temp file under /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/ (e.g. `SKY-006-review.md.tmp.<pid>`), then renamed to `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` — to prevent partial reads by downstream tooling. If the self-check fails, the agent MUST correct the document before performing the atomic write. If `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` already exists from a prior run, it MUST be fully overwritten (not appended to) by the atomic rename; the agent MUST NOT open the existing file in append mode at any point.
