stories.title: API Discovery: Execute Curl Probes, Capture Raw Results, Enforce Security Hardening
stories.description: Execute live curl probes against skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com using the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable. This child story covers the prerequisite gate, probe execution, abort conditions, raw result capture, file-permission hardening, secret-scrubbing scope, and execution-discipline invariants (exit codes, re-run behavior, filename sanitization, HTTP method invariance, stdout/stderr separation) only. No documentation writing occurs here — raw probe outputs are written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/ as intermediate artifacts for SKY-001b-2. Do NOT write any TypeScript, JavaScript, or compiled output. SECURITY HARDENING: this story enforces a no-write-to-repository constraint (AC11), a secret non-leakage / env-var scrubbing scope (AC12), and restrictive file permissions on probe artifacts (AC14); all three require human-review confirmation before SKY-002 unblock. ABORT PATHS: total-404 and zero-probes abort cases are merged into AC4 and require human-review of negative verification coverage (AC5); an additional all-curl-errors abort case is flagged for coordinator decision. FIVE HUMAN-REVIEW ITEMS BLOCKING SKY-002: (a) AC2 candidate endpoint set; (b) AC4 all-curl-errors abort branch classification; (c) AC5 negative-verification check list; (d) AC12 env-var scrubbing scope (which env vars beyond RAPIDAPI_KEY require redaction); (e) AC14 file-permission mode (whether 0644 is acceptable for read-only derived files). NO SPLIT: this story contains 19 ACs (above the 12-AC threshold), but the parent rule 'Never split a story that is already a split child' (splitDepth=1) suppresses the mandatory split — this is the documented no-split justification. AC15 exit-code contract was repaired in this scaffold (prior draft was truncated mid-sentence). DOWNSTREAM BLOCKER: this story blocks SKY-002; SKY-002 cannot begin until gate-result.txt, all probe-*.txt files, probe-summary.txt, and (if applicable) discovery-failure.md are written, exit codes are confirmed, and the five human-review items above are resolved.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 — PREREQUISITE GATE — VALUE & WHITESPACE: Before any other action, verify that the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is set and its trimmed value has length greater than zero. A value consisting solely of whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines) is treated as empty and triggers the identical abort behavior. If unset, empty, or whitespace-only, write the exact message 'RAPIDAPI_KEY is not set — aborting discovery' to stderr, exit with code 1 (per AC15), and perform NO further action — no directory creation, no file writes, no curl invocations, no network calls. The /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/gate-result.txt file is written ONLY on the success path; its content is exactly one line — 'PASS: RAPIDAPI_KEY is set' — followed by a single trailing newline. The earlier-draft example 'FAIL: RAPIDAPI_KEY is not set' as a gate-result.txt line is INCORRECT: on gate failure, the file is not created at all; the FAIL message is emitted to stderr only. The abort message MUST be the first and only line of stderr; no other progress chatter may be emitted before or instead of it on the gate-failure branch.

AC2 — EXECUTION SEQUENCE ORDER [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: On successful gate pass, execute the probe-execution sequence in this exact order and no other: (1) gate check on RAPIDAPI_KEY (abort on failure per AC1); (2) create the probes output directory with `mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes` and chmod it to 0700 (per AC14 and AC23) — if this mkdir or chmod fails for any reason (permission denied, ENOSPC, EROFS, EPERM on chmod), write the OS error message to stderr prefixed with 'mkdir failed: ' and exit with code 3; (3) execute the probe-execution sequence in declaration order; (4) for each probe, no probe-*.txt file may be written until that probe's curl invocation has completed (success, error, or timeout); (5) write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-summary.txt per AC9 only after every probe-*.txt has been written; (6) apply the abort check per AC4/AC23; (7) exit with the code per AC15. Each probe's full output is written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-<sanitized-path>.txt per AC17's sanitization rules. The exact candidate endpoint set is flagged for coordinator confirmation (see acFlagged).

AC3 — PROBE EXECUTION ROBUSTNESS: Each curl invocation MUST include a hard timeout (--max-time 15, per AC13) and MUST NOT use --fail / -f (which would suppress HTTP error response bodies); the --fail-with-body semantics are not available in the project's pinned curl version, so the implementation relies on capturing all output unconditionally. If curl exits non-zero for any reason (network error subsequent lines MUST contain the captured curl stderr (one or more lines, each beginning with 'curl: ' or the literal curl error text). The curl exit code MUST be captured and written to the probe file as a final comment line in the form '# curl_exit=<N>'. This format allows AC4's abort logic to distinguish 'curl failed to execute' from 'endpoint returned HTTP status' (per AC6's first-line extraction) and ensures no silent gaps in the probe record.

AC4 — ABORT ON TOTAL 404 OR ZERO PROBES COMPLETED [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: After all probes complete, inspect each probe file's first line for the HTTP status code. The story aborts (exit code 2 per AC15) before SKY-001b-2 begins in EITHER of the following two cases: (A) every probe that produced a real HTTP response returned 404 (zero working endpoints, where 'working' is per AC7 and AC8) — note that the synthetic first line 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR' does NOT count as a 404 for this purpose; OR (B) zero probe-*.txt files were written (no probe invocation produced any output file, including curl-error files from AC3 — this would only occur if all curl invocations were skipped or killed before reaching the write step). On abort, write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/discovery-failure.md containing on separate lines: (i) the current ISO 8601 date in the format 'Date: <ISO 8601>' (UTC, per AC22); (ii) the header 'Probed URLs:' followed by one URL per line; (iii) the header 'Observed Statuses:' followed by one status string per probe file (e.g. 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found' or 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR') in execution order; (iv) a blank line; (v) the exact message 'No working endpoints found — SKY-001b cannot produce a valid contract. Human review required before SKY-002 proceeds.' No api-contract.md may be created on this branch. discovery-failure.md MUST also satisfy AC14 (0600 mode) and AC12 (no key value). The all-curl-errors case (every probe is 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR') is NOT covered by case (A) as written; AC23 introduces a broader criterion and supersedes this AC's case (A) when the two conflict — the case-(A) language here is preserved verbatim for the canonical-404 case but the abort trigger in implementation is the AC23 rule. Flagged for coordinator decision (see acFlagged).

AC5 — NEGATIVE VERIFICATION ON ABORT PATHS [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: A human reviewer MUST confirm, before SKY-002 is unblocked, that the abort-path artifacts satisfy the following baseline checks: (i) /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/discovery-failure.md exists, has mode 0600 (per AC14), and contains the ISO date (UTC, per AC22), the full list of probed URLs, the full list of observed statuses, the blank line, and the exact abort message; (ii) /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-summary.txt is either absent OR its first line is exactly 'aborted — see discovery-failure.md' (no Markdown table, no counts); (iii) no api-contract.md exists anywhere under /tmp/skyscanner-app/; (iv) /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/gate-result.txt's first line is either 'PASS: RAPIDAPI_KEY is set' (abort reached via all-404, not via gate) or the file does not exist (abort reached via gate failure); (v) the literal value of RAPIDAPI_KEY does not appear in any artifact on the abort path (per AC12). The exact final list of negative checks is open for coordinator expansion before sign-off.

AC6 — PROBE FILE FORMAT: Each /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-<sanitized-path>.txt file's first line is the full HTTP status line as emitted by `curl -si` (e.g. 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK', 'HTTP/2 429', or the synthetic 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR' per AC3) followed by a single trailing newline. The observed HTTP status code MUST be extractable by reading only the first line of the file. No BOM, no leading whitespace before the status line, no extra blank lines between the status line and the first header. The file MUST be valid UTF-8 (no stray bytes from a binary response that would break downstream grep/awk). The file MUST end with exactly one trailing newline.

AC7 — WORKING-ENDPOINT CRITERION: A probed path is recorded as 'Working: yes' if any probe against it returns a 2xx status code or a 429 (Too Many Requests) status code, since both confirm the path exists and the subscription is active. A path is recorded as 'Working: no' if every probe against it returned 404, a curl error (per AC3), or a 3xx redirect (per AC8). Endpoints on sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com MUST NOT be probed (this host returns 404 for all paths and is excluded by design). Other RapidAPI hosts (e.g., sky-scanner.p.rapidapi.com, skyscanner-default.p.rapidapi.com) MUST NOT be probed unless explicitly added to the coordinator-confirmed endpoint set in AC2. The Working classification is per-path, not per-row: if the same path is probed multiple times, the 'Working' column value MUST be identical for every row of that path (see AC24).

AC8 — WORKING-ENDPOINT CRITERION — NON-STANDARD STATUSES: For HTTP status codes not explicitly addressed by AC7, the classification is: (a) 3xx (redirects, including 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) — treated as 'Working: no' because `curl -si` without -L does not follow them, and the redirect target is not validated by this spike; (b) 401 (Unauthorized) and 403 (Forbidden) — treated as 'Working: yes' because the path exists and the subscription is recognized, even if the specific endpoint is not entitled under the current key; (c) 5xx (server error, including 500, 502, 503, 504) — treated as 'Working: yes' because the path exists and was reached by the upstream gateway, regardless of upstream failure. Only 404, curl errors (per AC3), and 3xx (per (a)) are treated as definitively 'Working: no'. The observed status code is ALWAYS recorded verbatim in the probe-summary.txt table (per AC9) regardless of classification. Note: the all-curl-errors case is flagged for coordinator decision (see acFlagged) on whether it should also trigger the AC4 abort branch — AC23 introduces a unified rule that classifies it as 'zero Working: yes' and therefore abort.

AC9 — SUMMARY FILE: After all probes complete (and ONLY after every probe-*.txt has been written), write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-summary.txt containing, in this exact order: (a) a Markdown table whose header row is EXACTLY '| Host | Path | HTTP Method | Observed Status | Working (yes/no) |' followed by a header separator row EXACTLY '|---|---|---|---|---|---|' (six columns, six separators), followed by one row per probe file written (in the order probes were executed), with cells separated by pipe characters and one space on each side of the cell content; (b) a blank line; (c) the line 'Timestamp: <ISO 8601>' where <ISO 8601> is the current date-time in ISO 8601 format with the UTC 'Z' suffix (per AC22); (d) the line 'Counts: total=<N> working_yes=<N>' where <N> are non-negative integers. The file MUST end with a single trailing newline. The table MUST be valid GitHub-flavored Markdown. The 'Working (yes/no)' column reflects the per-path classification per AC7/AC8, applied uniformly to every row of that path (per AC24).

AC10 — FORBIDDEN FILES (extensions & manifests): This story MUST NOT create, modify, or write to any file with extension .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .tsbuildinfo, or to package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.json, .npmrc, .env, .env.*, or any other dependency manifest, lockfile, or build configuration file. The only files this story may produce under /tmp/skyscanner-app/ are: gate-result.txt, probe-*.txt files (one per probe), probe-summary.txt, and conditionally discovery-failure.md (only on the abort path per AC4/AC23, never on the success path). No symbolic links, hard links, FIFOs, or other special filesystem entries may be created under /tmp/skyscanner-app/ by this story.

AC11 — FORBIDDEN WRITES TO REPOSITORY: No source files, no test files, no configuration files, and no documentation files in the repository (i.e., any file under version control outside the /tmp/skyscanner-app/ tree) may be created, modified,l, .sh, and dotfiles. Reading from the repository (e.g., sourcing a config file) is permitted; only writes are forbidden. The story MUST NOT create or modify any symlink whose target is inside the repository tree.

AC12 — SECRET NON-LEAKAGE & ENV-VAR SCRUBBING SCOPE [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: The literal value of the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable MUST NOT appear in any file produced by this story — not in gate-result.txt, not in any probe-*.txt file, not in probe-summary.txt, and not in discovery-failure.md. The key MUST NOT appear in any process's argv (e.g., visible to other users via `ps aux`), in any shell history file (e.g., ~/.bash_history, ~/.zsh_history), or in any core dump. The key is passed to curl exclusively via the -H 'X-RapidAPI-Key: <value>' header using a curl config file (-K /path/to/curl.cfg) so the key never appears in argv or in any process listing; alternatively, the key may be passed via stdin using a heredoc piped to curl, with the same non-argv requirement. If a probe response body echoes the key value (e.g., in an upstream error message), that response body is still written verbatim to the probe-*.txt file, but the key value is masked or redacted in any DERIVED or SUMMARY output (probe-summary.txt, discovery-failure.md) by replacing it with the string '***REDACTED***'. Stderr redaction is governed by AC21. SCOPE CLARIFICATION [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: the default env-var scrubbing scope is RAPIDAPI_KEY only; the coordinator MUST confirm before SKY-002 unblock whether additional env vars (e.g., HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY, custom auth headers, other RapidAPI headers like X-RapidAPI-Host, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD) require the same redaction in derived/summary output.

AC13 — CURL TIMEOUT ENFORCEMENT: Every curl probe invocation MUST include a bounded execution time of EXACTLY --max-time 15 (15 seconds, EXACTLY 15, not 14, not 16). If --max-time fires, curl exits with code 28 and emits 'curl: (28) Operation timed out' (or the localized equivalent) to stderr. The probe file's first line MUST be exactly 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR' and subsequent lines MUST contain curl's timeout error. If --connect-timeout fires (a subset of max-time, exit code 7 or 28), the same handling applies. After a timed-out probe, the next probe proceeds — the timed-out endpoint is NOT retried within the same run. A test that asserts the absence of any curl invocation exceeding 20 seconds wall-clock (allowing for cleanup) is the canonical regression check. The --max-time flag MUST be passed as a separate argv element (not concatenated with the URL) to ensure it is not silently swallowed by shell parsing.

AC14 — FILE PERMISSIONS FOR PROBE ARTIFACTS [REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW]: Probe artifact files (gate-result.txt, probe-*.txt, probe-summary.txt, discovery-failure.md) MUST be created with restrictive file permissions to prevent other users on the host from reading API responses, which may echo sensitive content (auth state, request IDs, internal paths, or — rarely — key material). Default mode for files: 0600 (owner read/write only, no group, no other). The probes directory /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes MUST also be created with mode 0700. The implementation MUST verify the mode after each write (e.g., `stat -c '%a' file` returns '600' for files and '700' for the directory); a file mode of 0644 or a directory mode of 0755 is a hard failure of this AC. If a pre-existing probes directory has the wrong mode, the implementation MUST chmod it to 0700 before writing any file into it (per AC23). Coordinator MUST confirm exact mode and whether 0644 is acceptable as an alternative for read-only derived files such as probe-summary.txt before SKY-002 unblock. Implementation note: setting `umask 077` at the start of the spike is the canonical mechanism to ensure default file-creation modes inherit 0600; an explicit `chmod 0600 file` after each write is also acceptable.

AC15 — EXIT CODE CONTRACT: This story's process exit code is the single source of truth for downstream automation (CI pipelines, the SKY-001b-2 trigger) to determine which branch to execute. The contract is: exit code 0 on the success path (gate passed, at least one probe file written, probe-summary.txt written, and at least one probe classified as 'Working: yes' per AC7/AC8); exit code 1 on gate failure (per AC1); exit code 2 on the abort path (per AC4/AC23); exit code 3 on infrastructure failure such as mkdir or chmod failure (per AC2/AC23) or other unexpected OS errors (ENOSPC, EROFS, EACCES on a file write); exit codes 4-125 reserved for future use; exit codes 126/127 reserved for shell-level failures (command not found, not executable) and MUST NOT be used by this story's logic. A test that runs the story with deliberately crafted inputs for each branch (unset key, all-404, mkdir failure, healthy run) and asserts the process exit code matches the contract above is the canonical regression check. The success path's 'Working: yes' precondition is evaluated AFTER AC23's broader abort criterion; i.e., a run with no working endpoints exits 2, not 0, even if probe files were written. [REQUIRES COORDINATOR REVIEW — see acFlagged.]

AC16 — PROBE RE-RUN BEHAVIOR: Re-executing this story (e.g., for re-probing after rate-limit recovery, after a transient network failure, or for re-validation with a rotated RAPIDAPI_KEY) overwrites gate-result.txt, each probe-*.txt file, probe-summary.txt, and (if produced) discovery-failure.md with the new run's results. The probes directory is reused; existing files are replaced in place, not merged or appended to. A successful re-run that produces at least one 'Working: yes' result does NOT delete a pre-existing discovery-failure.md from a prior aborted run — that file persists as historical evidence. If the new run also aborts, the new discovery-failure.md overwrites the prior one. No backup, snapshot, or rollback of prior artifacts is performed. The implementation MUST tolerate stale probe-*.txt files from a prior run (e.g., a different endpoint set) by overwriting or by detecting and removing them at the start of the new run; the chosen strategy is open to the implementer. A test that runs the story twice with different RAPIDAPI_KEY values and asserts that probe-summary.txt reflects only the second run's timestamps and counts is the canonical regression check.

AC17 — PROBE FILENAME SANITIZATION: The <sanitized-path> segment of probe-<sanitized-path>.txt is derived from the probed URL's path component (and query string, if present) by applying, in this exact order: (1) replace every '/' with '-'; (2) replace every '?' with '-q-'; (3) replace every '&' with '-and-'; (4) replace every '=' with '-'; (5) replace any character not in [a-zA-Z0-9._-] with a single '-'; (6) collapse consecutive '-' characters into a single '-'; (7) strip leading and trailing '-'. The sanitization function MUST be deterministic — the same input URL always produces the same filename. The resulting filename MUST NOT exceed 200 characters; if the natural sanitized name exceeds 200 characters, the path is truncated at 191 characters and suffixed with '-' followed by an 8-character lowercase hexadecimal hash of the full original path (e.g., 'probe-<truncated>-<hash>.txt'). The fragment component (everything after '#') of the URL MUST be stripped before sanitization. Edge cases: an empty path (URL 'https://host') sanitizes to 'probe-root.txt'; a path consisting of only '/' sanitizes to 'probe-root.txt'; a path with only unsafe characters sanitizes to 'probe-h-<hash>.txt' (the hash disambiguates). Examples: '/flights/search' → 'probe-flights-search.txt'; '/v1/flights?from=NYC&to=LAX' → 'probe-v1-flights-q-from-NYC-and-to-LAX.txt'. [Hash algorithm and edge-case rules require coordinator confirmation — see acFlagged.]

AC18 — HTTP METHOD INVARIANCE: Every probe MUST use HTTP method GET. The 'HTTP Method' column in the probe-summary.txt table is therefore ALWAYS the literal string 'GET' on every row. The implementation MUST NOT use -X, --request, or any other flag that would change the HTTP method. If a future story requires a non-GET probe (POST, PUT, DELETE), that is a story split, not an in-story change. This invariant is testable by reading probe-summary.txt and asserting every row's 'HTTP Method' cell equals 'GET' exactly.

AC19 — STDOUT/STDERR DISCIPLINE: Human-readable progress and status messages — gate pass/fail, mkdir result, probe start/complete announcements, abort messages, discovery-failure.md write confirmation, summary write confirmation, exit code summary — are written to stderr ONLY and is expected to be empty for this spike; if stdout is non-empty, the test fixture comparison will fail. This separation ensures that piping the script's stdout (e.g., `tee` for CI logging) does not corrupt any file artifact, and that file artifacts are deterministic strings not interleaved with progress chatter. A test that captures the script's stdout to /dev/null and asserts that the four canonical files are byte-for-byte identical to a reference fixture is the canonical regression check. Stderr text is also governed by AC21 (no key material) and AC24 (no ANSI escapes).

AC20 — CURL INVOCATION FLAG RESTRICTIONS: To preserve security (no key leakage) and response fidelity (no silent transformations), every curl probe invocation MUST be invoked with ONLY the following flags plus the target URL: --max-time 15 (per AC13), -si (show headers, silent, per AC6), -H 'X-RapidAPI-Key: <value>' (per AC12), -H 'X-RapidAPI-Host: skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com' (per the host defined in AC2's endpoint set), and -K /path/to/curl.cfg (per AC12) OR the equivalent stdin-heredoc mechanism. The following flags are EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN in any probe invocation: -v / --verbose (would echo the -H header value to stderr in cleartext, violating AC12/AC21); -k / --insecure (would silently accept invalid TLS, hiding a class of network failures); -L / --location (would follow redirects and overwrite the first-line status code defined in AC6); --proxy / -x (would route the request through a host not on the allowlist, potentially leaking the key); --user / -u (basic-auth fallback, not used by this spike); -b / --cookie (would persist cookies across probes); --cert / --key (client mTLS, not used by this spike). A test that greps the script source for these forbidden flag spellings is the canonical regression check.

AC21 — STDERR REDACTION DISCIPLINE: The literal value of the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable MUST NOT appear in any line written to stderr by this story's logic. Specifically: (a) the stderr message emitted on a curl error MUST NOT echo the -H 'X-RapidAPI-Key: <value>' header value (some curl builds print the full header set on certain errors); (b) any diagnostic message emitted by the story's wrapper script (e.g., 'probe failed: <URL>') MUST be constructed such that the key is not interpolated; (c) if curl emits a header value to stderr, the wrapper MUST pipe stderr through a sed/awk pass that replaces the key with '***REDACTED***' before writing to the final stderr stream. A test that runs the story with a known-sentinel RAPIDAPI_KEY value (e.g., 'TEST-SENTINEL-DO-NOT-USE') and greps all captured stderr for the sentinel is the canonical regression check. The redaction string '***REDACTED***' is the same as in AC12.

AC22 — TIMESTAMP FORMAT (UTC Z): All ISO 8601 timestamps emitted by this story (in gate-result.txt's PASS line, in probe-summary.txt's 'Timestamp:' line per AC9, in discovery-failure.md's 'Date:' line per AC4) MUST be in UTC and MUST end with the literal 'Z' suffix (e.g., '2026-06-23T11:12:31Z'). Local-time timestamps (with offsets like '-07:00' or without any zone designator) are NOT acceptable. The format MUST be second-precision; sub-second precision is allowed but not required. The 'date' command invocation on the host MUST use 'date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' or equivalent. A test that asserts the timestamp matches the regex '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$' is the canonical regression check.

AC23 — MIXED-STATUS ABORT CLARIFICATION & DIRECTORY STATE RECOVERY: This AC supersedes the literal text of AC4 case (A) where the two conflict. The unified abort criterion is: the story MUST abort (exit code 2 per AC15) if and only if zero probe-*.txt files reflect a path with Working: yes per AC7/AC8. Concretely: (i) if every probe file's first line is 'HTTP/0 0 CURL_ERROR' (all curl errors), abort — this is the previously-unaddressed case openspec flagged in AC4/AC8; (ii) if every probe that produced a real HTTP response returned 404, abort; (iii) if the mix is some 404s and some curl_errors and at least one real 2xx/429/401/403/5xx, proceed to the success path; (iv) if the mix is 404s and 3xx and no curl errors, abort. Additionally, this AC governs directory state recovery: if /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes exists with mode != 0700, the implementation MUST chmod it to 0700 (per AC14) before writing the first file; if the directory does not exist, mkdir -p creates it with mode 0700. The chmod failure path (EACCES, EPERM) is a code-3 infrastructure failure (per AC15). Flagged for coordinator confirmation of the broader abort rule (see acFlagged).

AC24 — PLAIN-TEXT STDERR (NO ANSI ESCAPES): All bytes written to stderr by this story MUST be plain ASCII (or valid UTF-8 without ANSI escape sequences). Specifically, no CSI sequences ('\x1b['), no SGR color codes, no cursor-position escapes, no OSC sequences, and no BEL characters may appear in any stderr line. The exit-code summary, probe-start announcements, and abort messages MUST be greppable with simple tools. This AC complements AC19 (stderr/file separation) by ensuring stderr is also log-analysis-friendly and screen-reader-friendly. A test that captures the script's stderr and asserts no byte matches the regex '\x1b\[' is the canonical regression check. Any future enhancement to add color MUST be gated behind an explicit TTY-detection check and a --color flag, not enabled by default.

stories.description: Using the raw probe outputs produced by SKY-001b-1 (in /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/), write the authoritative /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md. This story covers all documentation curl probes. Do NOT write any TypeScript, JavaScript, or compiled output. acceptanceCriteria: Host section: api-contract.md contains a 'Host' section that records the confirmed x-rapidapi-host value (must be skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com) and the observed HTTP status code sourced from probe-summary.txt. A 429 response is sufficient proof of an active subscription.

Endpoints section: api-contract.md contains an 'Endpoints' section listing at least one working endpoint (2xx or 429 observed) with HTTP method, full path, and observed status. Paths returning only 404 must not be listed. Paths on sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com must not appear.

Authentication section: api-contract.md contains an 'Authentication' section documenting x-rapidapi-key and x-rapidapi-host as required headers. The placeholder '$RAPIDAPI_KEY' must be used consistently throughout the entire document — in the Authentication section, in any sample request blocks, in sample-response reconstruction notes, and in the key-safety scan commentary — wherever a key value would otherwise appear; no other placeholder format and no literal key substring longer than 4 characters is permitted in any section.

Query Parameters section: api-contract.md contains a 'Query Parameters' section enumerating every parameter observed in successful probe requests, each marked as required or optional, with at least one concrete example value per parameter.

Sample Response section: api-contract.md contains a 'Sample Response' section that branches on probe-summary.txt outcome. (a) If a live 2xx body was captured, include a JSON snippet showing the top-level structure and at least one flight result object. (b) If only 429 responses were captured, include the raw 429 body and an explicit note 'Flight result shape inferred from documentation'. The section also includes a 'FlightResult Field Mapping' table that maps price, origin, destination, departureTime, arrivalTime, carrier, and durationMinutes to specific API JSON fields or explicitly marks them as absent or inferred.

Discovery Metadata section: api-contract.md contains a 'Discovery Metadata' section with the ISO 8601 date the probes were run, and a Markdown table with columns [Host, Path, HTTP Method, Observed Status] sourced from probe-summary.txt — exactly one row per probe.

Key-safety scan: before declaring the story complete, the file is scanned to confirm the literal RAPIDAPI_KEY value does not appear anywhere — only the placeholder '$RAPIDAPI_KEY' is permitted, and no key-like substring longer than 4 characters may be present in the body, headers, or sample payloads.

Inferred-contract risk disclosure: when probe-summary.txt shows only 429 responses (no 2xx), api-contract.md contains a clearly labeled 'Inferred Contract Risk' notice stating that the FlightResult field mappings are inferred from documentation rather than confirmed by live 2xx responses, and that the human coordinator must accept this risk before SKY-002 implementation begins. When at least one 2xx was captured, this notice is omitted.

Human-acceptance gate (tool-enforced JSON contract): when probe-summary.txt shows only 429 responses, the file /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/acceptance_gate.json is produced alongside api-contract.md and contains exactly these keys with the defined types — 'inferred_contract_risk' (boolean), 'acknowledged_by' (non-empty string identifying the human coordinator), 'acknowledged_at_iso8601' (ISO 8601 timestamp), and 'gate_passed' (boolean, true). The file's existence, schema, and gate_passed value form a machine-readable contract that downstream tooling MUST validate by JSON-parsing. SKY-002 implementation tooling MUST refuse to start — hard-enforced, not a warning, with no override flag, no exception path, and no warning-suppression mechanism — if this file is absent, if gate_passed is false, or if acknowledged_by is empty; on refusal, tooling exits non-zero with a message naming the failed condition. When at least one 2xx was captured, the file is either omitted entirely or present with inferred_contract_risk: false and gate_passed: true.

stories.title: API Discovery: Execute Curl Probes and Capture Raw Results
stories.description: Execute live curl probes against skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com using the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable. This child story covers the prerequisite gate, probe execution, abort conditions, and raw result capture only. No documentation writing occurs here — raw probe outputs are written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/ as intermediate artifacts for SKY-001b-2. Do NOT write any TypeScript, JavaScript, or compiled output.
acceptanceCriteria: PREREQUISITE GATE: Before any other action, check that the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is set and non-empty. Write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/gate-result.txt in ALL cases: on pass, content is exactly 'GATE: PASS — RAPIDAPI_KEY is set and non-empty'; on abort, content is exactly 'GATE: FAIL — RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent or empty'. If the gate fails, write the abort message 'RAPIDAPI_KEY is not set — aborting discovery' to stderr and halt immediately — no curl probes, directory creation beyond the gate file, or additional file writes may occur.

IDEMPOTENCY: If /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/ already exists from a prior run, clear its contents (e.g. rm -rf /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/* or equivalent) before writing any new probe files. No stale probe files from a previous run may persist alongside new probe files after a successful gate pass.

PROBE SEQUENCE: Execute steps in this exact order: (1) verify RAPIDAPI_KEY is non-empty (gate check above), (2) mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes, (3) execute two or more curl -si --max-time 30 probes against distinct candidate endpoint paths on skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com. Each probe must include an explicit --max-time flag (value between 10 and 60 seconds inclusive). Each probe's full output (status line + headers + body) is written to a separate file under /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/ named by sanitized path (e.g. probe-flights-search.txt). No probe output file may be written before its corresponding probe command has exited.

ABORT CONDITION — ALL 404s: If every probed endpoint returns HTTP 404, abort without proceeding to SKY-001b-2. Write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/discovery-failure.md containing: (a) the ISO 8601 timestamp of the abort, (b) all probed URLs, (c) all observed HTTP status codes, and (d) the message 'No working endpoints found — SKY-001b cannot produce a valid contract. Human review required before SKY-002 proceeds.' Do not create api-contract.md in this case.

PROBE FILE CONTENT: Each file in /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/ (excluding gate-result.txt and probe-summary.txt) must contain the complete curl -si output for its probe: the HTTP status line as the first line (format: 'HTTP/1.x NNN <reason>'), all response headers, a blank line, and the complete response body. The HTTP status code must be parseable from the first line of the file.

STATUS CODE INTERPRETATION: A 429 (Too Many Requests) response is accepted as proof that the probed path exists and the subscription is active. A 2xx response is also accepted as working. Any path that returns only 404 across all probes is recorded as non-working. Paths on sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com must never be probed.

PROBE SUMMARY FILE: After all probes complete (and only if the gate passed and not all probes returned 404), write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/probes/probe-summary.txt. The file must contain: (a) a pipe-delimited Markdown table with exactly these columns in this order — Host | Path | HTTP Method | Observed Status | Working (yes/no) — with one data row per probe, a header row, and a separator row using the pattern |---|---|---|---|---|; followed by (b) on a new line, the output of `curl --version` prefixed with 'curl-version: '. This exact schema is the downstream contract consumed by SKY-001b-2 and must not deviate.

NO CODE ARTIFACTS: No TypeScript, JavaScript, compiled output, package.json, lockfiles, or any dependency manifest files are created or modified as part of this story. All actions are performed via shell commands (curl, mkdir, rm, echo, etc.) only.

A 429 (Too Many Requests) on an endpoint confirms the path is valid — document it. The goal is an accurate contract doc, not a working implementation. When `searchFlights` resolves with one or more results, stdout contains: (a) a header row with columns Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops joined by ` | `; (b) a separator row where each segment is exactly as many `-` characters as that column's padded width, segments joined by ` | `; (c) one data row per result with columns joined by ` | `. When `searchFlights` resolves with an empty array, stdout contains exactly the single line `No flights found.` (no trailing whitespace, single trailing newline) and the process exits 0.

When multiple validation errors are present in a single run, only the first one encountered is reported and the exit code is determined by that first error alone. The file ends with `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` — no unconditional `main()` invocation.

If `renderTable(results)` throws (or rejects), `cli.ts` writes the thrown error's `message` to stderr and exits 1, consistent with all other error handling paths. `cli.ts` does not silently swallow or re-throw rendering errors.

`cli.ts` imports `SkyscannerClient` from `./skyscanner/client` (NOT `./skyscanner-client`) and imports `renderTable` from `./table`. The client is constructed as `new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey })` and `searchFlights` is invoked with `{ origin, destination, date, adults }` using the validated argument fields. `cli.ts` does not write or modify `cli.test.ts`.

stories.description: Implement `src/table.ts` exporting `renderTable(flights: Flight[], currency?: string): string`. The function is pure (no I/O). Column order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Dynamic width computation, left-align non-Price columns, right-align Price column, LF-joined rows, no trailing newline, empty-array returns `'No flights found.'`. Wire into existing `src/cli.ts`: pass Flight[] and currency option to renderTable, write result to stdout. HUMAN_REVIEW: confirm rejection-path ownership against SKY-003a before building.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/table.ts` exists, exports `renderTable(flights: Flight[], currency?: string): string`, imports the `Flight` type from the existing types module (from SKY-002) without redeclaring it, and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors; field access uses typed property names (`flight.airline`, `flight.price`, etc.) so TypeScript surfaces compile-time errors on property renames — no string-keyed dynamic access; `src/table.ts` must not import from `src/cli.ts` (dependency is strictly `cli.ts` → `table.ts`); the currency symbol is concatenated as a plain string with no `eval`, `Function()`, or dynamic code execution

Header row columns appear in exactly this order: `Airline`, `Price`, `Departure`, `Arrival`, `Duration`, `Stops`; cells are joined by ` | ` (one space, pipe, one space); the row has no leading and no trailing `|`; for every non-Price column W = `Math.max(header.length, max(value.toString().length for all rows))`; no locale-aware formatting (`toLocaleString`, `toFixed`, thousands separators) is applied to any non-Price field; for the Price column each cell is formatted as `<symbol><price.toString()>` and W = `Math.max('Price'.length, max(formattedPrice.length for all rows))` — a multi-character symbol such as `'USD'` contributes its full length to W
The separator row contains exactly 6 segments joined by ` | ` with no leading or trailing `|`; each segment is exactly W hyphens for that column's computed W with no spaces inside the segment

All non-Price columns are left-aligned: each cell value (header and data) is padded with trailing spaces to width W; no leading spaces on non-Price cells; when a data cell converts to empty string via `.toString()` the cell is rendered as W trailing spaces and W is at least the header length for that column

Price column is right-aligned: each formatted price string is padded with leading spaces to width W; the header label `Price` is also padded with leading spaces to W; no trailing spaces on Price cells; when `price` is `0` the formatted cell is `<symbol>0` — zero must never be treated as falsy or replaced by the default symbol
Currency symbol: when `currency` is a non-empty string it is used verbatim (including multi-character symbols); when `currency` is absent, `undefined`, `null`, or `''` the symbol defaults to `£`
`renderTable([])` returns the exact string `'No flights found.'` (strict equality, length 17, no newline, no leading/trailing whitespace) — no header, separator, or data rows are produced

The returned string for non-empty input is header row, separator row, and one data row per flight joined by `\n` (LF, U+000A — not CRLF) with no leading newline and no trailing newline; splitting by `\n` yields exactly `2 + flights.length` elements; `renderTable` is a pure function and must not call `console.log`, `process.stdout.write`, `process.exit`, or perform any I/O or side effects; `src/cli.ts` passes the `Flight[]` result of `searchFlights` and any `currency` CLI option to `renderTable` then writes the returned string to stdout via a single `console.log` or `process.stdout.write` call with no additional formatting [HUMAN_REVIEW: confirm whether searchFlights rejection → stderr + exit 1 is already owned by SKY-003a; if not, add: when `searchFlights` rejects, `src/cli.ts` writes the rejection `.message` (or string representation when no `.message`) to stderr, exits with code `1`, and writes nothing to stdout]

stories.title: Implement src/server.ts — Express app skeleton, route handlers, and package.json wiring
stories.description: Implement the Express HTTP server in src/server.ts. Import SkyscannerClient and FlightResult from './skyscanner/client' (SKY-002 export). Expose a named `app` export separate from the listen() call. Guard listen() with `require.main === module` (CJS project — do NOT use import.meta). Register /health, /, /search, and /cheapest routes with all validation and error handling described in ACs. Create src/public/index.html. Wire package.json 'start' and 'build' scripts. Only use installed packages: express, @types/express, typescript, tsup, vitest, supertest, @types/supertest. Do NOT import helmet, morgan, uuid, cors, compression, or any uninstalled package. Do NOT add req.id or requestId middleware. DEFERRED: CORS headers and query-injection hardening are explicitly out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call; the `listen()` call is guarded with `if (require.main === module)` — this project emits CJS (verify via tsup.config.ts or the `tsup` field in package.json before coding); do NOT use import.meta.url or any ESM-only pattern

The `from` query param is mapped to `SearchParams.origin` and the `to` query param is mapped to `SearchParams.destination` when constructing the object passed to SkyscannerClient.search() — no other key names are used; this mapping must be explicit in src/server.ts source (e.g. `origin: req.query.from`) and must not silently forward wrong keys

GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }; GET /health is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY and returns HTTP 200 regardless of whether the env var is set or absent

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type matching text/html and response body equal to the contents of src/public/index.html; this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY; src/public/index.html exists and contains valid HTML (non-empty file with an <html> root element)

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected

GET /search and GET /cheapest each validate required params (from, to, date): missing or empty-string values return HTTP 400 application/json { error: string }; the `date` param is validated against /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ and non-conforming values (e.g. '01-08-2026', 'tomorrow', '2026-8-1') return HTTP 400; the `adults` param is optional (defaults to 1) but when present must be a positive integer — non-numeric, zero, or negative values return HTTP 400; these validation rules are identical on both /search and /cheapest

GET /search with valid params returns HTTP 200 application/json body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string } where count strictly equals flights.length and searchedAt is a non-hardcoded ISO-8601 datetime string; GET /cheapest with valid params returns HTTP 200 with the single FlightResult whose price is ≤ every other result, or HTTP 404 application/json { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array; when SkyscannerClient throws, both routes return HTTP 500 application/json { error: string } without crashing

MODIFICATIONS (5 ACs refined):
- AC3: harmonized Content-Type to 'matching application pattern. Same harmonization applied to AC5, AC6, AC7.
- AC5: added empty-string env var handling (RAPIDAPI_KEY='' is treated as 'not configured', equivalent to absent). Defensive against misconfigured deploys where the env var is set but blank.
- AC6: tightened `adults` validation. Original said 'positive integer — non-numeric, zero, or negative' which left gaps for '', '1.5', '1e2', ' 1' (whitespace), etc. Revised to require parsing as a finite positive integer via Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1 (or equivalent). Also added semantic date validation: the regex /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ matches invalid dates like '2026-13-01' (month 13) and '2026-02-30' (Feb 30) — these must also return 400. Implemented as 'parse and round-trip through Date, reject if input round-trip differs' or equivalent.
- AC7: made /search empty-array behavior explicit. The original AC specified the response shape `{ flights: FlightResult[] }` but did not state what happens when the array is empty, leaving ambiguity vs /cheapest's 404. Revised to 200 with `{ flights: [], count: 0, searchedAt: <ISO-8601> }` — only /cheapest returns 404 on empty. Also added 500 error message safety: the error string must be generic (e.g. 'Internal server error') and MUST NOT include the raw thrown error, stack trace, or any internal implementation details (security: avoid leaking client config, file paths, or third-party error shapes).
- AC9: clarified invalid PORT handling. Original said 'defaults to 3000 when PORT is absent or empty' but did not address PORT='abc' or PORT='3.14' (parseInt would yield NaN, which Express would reject). Revised to fall back to 3000 for any non-valid-integer PORT value.

stories.title: Implement src/server.ts: GET /search with validation, CORS, error handling
stories.description: Implement src/server.ts containing GET /search route with validation, CORS, error handling, and flight search functionality. The route validates from/to/date/adults query params (400 on invalid input), calls client.searchFlights({ origin, destination, date, adults }), and instantiates SkyscannerClient({}) inside each route handler (per-request, never at module level). CORS is implemented as inline middleware — the cors npm package is NOT used. A four-argument Express error-handling middleware handles unexpected rejections with HTTP 500. The listen call is guarded. The app instance is exported. No express.json() body-parsing middleware is added. No 503 middleware or RAPIDAPI_KEY check is added. Both npx tsc --noEmit must exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /search with all valid parameters (from, to, date as YYYY-MM-DD, adults as positive integer string) returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and a body containing { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string }, where count is strictly equal to the length of flights and searchedAt is a valid ISO-8601 datetime string.
GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when any of the required parameters (from, to, date) are missing, empty, or contain only whitespace.

GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the date parameter is present but does not match the pattern YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., contains letters, incorrect separators, or wrong length).

GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the adults parameter is present and is not a string consisting solely of ASCII digits (e.g., contains letters, signs, decimal points, exponents, leading zeros, or whitespace); if adults is absent or an empty string, it is treated as 1.
GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the adults parameter is present as a negative integer string.
GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the adults parameter is present as a string with leading zeros.
GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the date parameter is present with invalid day or month values (e.g., 2023-13-01, 2023-02-30).
GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: string } when the date parameter is present with a date before 1900-01-01.
GET /search returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and a body containing { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string } when the adults parameter is present as '0'.

CORS is enabled for all routes via inline middleware that sets the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to '*' for all responses, and HTTP OPTIONS requests are handled with a 204 No Content response and no response body.

A four-argument Express error-handling middleware is registered after all routes and catches unhandled errors, returning HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and a body { error: 'Internal Server Error' }; no route handler uses try/catch for this purpose.

The module uses export default app (or export { app }) to export the Express app instance before the listen guard; the listen call is wrapped in if (require.main === module) so tests can import the app without starting the server.
The SkyscannerClient class is imported from './skyscanner/client', and FlightResult is also imported from the same module; no import from './skyscanner/types' is present or required.
SkyscannerClient is instantiated inside each route handler per request, and not at the module level or as a singleton.
The server does not check for or depend on the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable, and does not include any 503 service unavailable middleware.
The TypeScript compilation succeeds with npx tsc --noEmit with zero errors and zero warnings.
GET /search with a valid date in the future (e.g., 2025-01-01) does not return HTTP 400 due to date being in the future.
GET /search with adults parameter as '999' returns HTTP 200 with valid response body, indicating no upper bound is enforced.

When an unhandled error is thrown in a route handler (e.g., TypeError from undefined property access), the server responds with HTTP 500 and { error: 'Internal Server Error' } without exposing stack traces or internal details.
The server responds with HTTP 400 and { error: string } when the from or to parameter contains non-ASCII characters or control characters.
The server responds with HTTP 400 and { error: string } when the date parameter contains Unicode calendar characters (e.g., Arabic numerals) instead of ASCII digits.
The server does not set any additional CORS headers beyond Access-Control-Allow-Origin, and does not include Access-Control-Allow-Credentials or Access-Control-Allow-Methods.

stories.title: HTML dashboard — structure, form, accessibility, and self-containment
stories.description: Implement the static structure of src/public/index.html: document metadata, the search form with all four fields and proper labelling, required-field validation, whitespace-trimming, accessible table markup, aria-live regions, and the self-containment constraint (no external CDN links). All CSS lives in a <style> block; all JS lives in a <script> block. This child covers everything that can be verified without issuing live network requests.
acceptanceCriteria: src/public/index.html exists and is served by the Express app via any valid mechanism (e.g. express.static(), res.sendFile(), or equivalent) such that a GET request to the root path '/' returns the file with Content-Type text/html

The document declares <meta charset='utf-8'>, contains <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'>, has a non-empty <title> element, and the root <html> element carries a lang attribute (e.g. lang='en')

The four search fields are contained in a <form> element; each field has a corresponding <label> associated via matching for/id attributes: From (type=text, placeholder indicating IATA code), To (type=text, placeholder indicating IATA code), Date (type=date), Adults (type=number, default value='1', min='1')

The From, To, and Date fields carry the native required attribute; submitting the form with any of those fields empty does NOT issue a network request — a validation message (native browser or inline) is shown instead, and event.preventDefault() is called so no full-page reload or URL navigation occurs

Field values for From and To are trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace before being encoded into query parameters; an input containing only whitespace is treated as empty and triggers the same validation message as a blank field, without issuing a network request

The results table uses <thead> containing <th scope='col'> elements for each column header (Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops) and a <tbody> for data rows so screen readers can associate cells with headers; the table is present in the DOM on page load (it may be hidden until results arrive)

Loading indicators and error message containers are placed in or associated with an aria-live='polite' region or role='alert' element so screen reader users are notified of state changes without requiring focus movement

The HTML file contains no <link rel='stylesheet' href='...'> pointing to external origins and no <script src='...'> pointing to external origins — all CSS is in one or more <style> blocks and all JS is in one or more <script> blocks within the single file

stories.title: HTML dashboard — dynamic behaviour, error handling, dark mode, and responsiveness
stories.description: Implement all runtime JavaScript behaviour and CSS visual features of src/public/index.html: fetch calls to /search and /cheapest, loading/disabled state management, AbortController-based request cancellation, XSS-safe DOM rendering, cheapest-row highlighting with accessible label, empty/error states, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme, and mobile responsiveness at 375px viewport width.
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting the form issues GET /search?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin with field values encoded via URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent; pressing Enter within any field triggers the same search as clicking the submit button; the 'Find Cheapest' button issues GET /cheapest?from=&to=&date=&adults= on the same origin passing the four current form field values, is rendered as a <button> element (not a <div> or <span>), and is keyboard-operable (focusable and activatable via Enter/Space)

The search submit button has the disabled attribute set while a /search request is in-flight and is re-enabled once the request resolves (success or error); the 'Find Cheapest' button has the disabled attribute set while a /cheapest request is in-flight and is re-enabled once it resolves — preventing duplicate concurrent requests for each respective action

A loading indicator (spinner or 'Searching…' text) is visible while a /search request is in-flight and is hidden (display:none or equivalent) once the request resolves; a separate or shared loading indicator is visible while a /cheapest request is in-flight and hidden once it resolves

On a successful /search response the results <tbody> is populated with one row per flight containing columns: Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops; if the response contains an empty flights array a 'No results found' (or equivalent) message is displayed and no stale rows or header-only empty table from a prior search remain visible; submitting a new search clears prior table rows and any existing cheapest highlight before rendering the new response

If /search returns an HTTP error or the fetch rejects (network failure) an error message is displayed inline in the UI (not only logged to the console); if /cheapest returns an HTTP error or the fetch rejects an error message is displayed inline in the UI; a previously displayed error message is cleared when the next /search or /cheapest request begins so stale error text does not persist alongside fresh results

The row in the results table matching the /cheapest response is visually distinguished (e.g. highlighted background or 'Cheapest' badge) and carries an accessible label (e.g. aria-label or a visually-hidden text node indicating it is the cheapest option); if no table results are currently displayed, the cheapest flight details (Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops) are shown in a separate clearly labelled summary section

All flight data from API responses is rendered using safe DOM methods (e.g. textContent, createElement, setAttribute) rather than by interpolating API-supplied strings directly into innerHTML — this prevents XSS if an upstream API field contains HTML or script content; when a second /search request is submitted while a prior /search request is still in-flight the earlier request is aborted via AbortController and its response is discarded; the same AbortController pattern applies to concurrent /cheapest requests — out-of-order responses must never overwrite results from a newer request

The page applies distinct background-color and color values when the OS/browser prefers dark mode via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) using CSS custom properties defined on :root; on a viewport width of 375px the form fields and results table are usable without horizontal scrolling of the page body — the table either scrolls horizontally within its own container (overflow-x: auto on a wrapper) or its columns reflow appropriately

stories.title: Implement src/cli.ts entry point with sentinel error handling
stories.description: Implement `src/cli.ts` as the sole owner of process-exit and stderr responsibilities per parent AC-5. Exports exactly: `parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments`, `validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments`, and `async main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>`. `main()` MUST catch any `Error` whose `message` matches `^exit:[0-9]+$` and call `process.exit(N)`; construct `new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey })`; call `searchFlights({ origin, destination, date, adults })`; render via `renderTable` imported from `./table`; print `No flights found.` (single trailing newline) and return (exit 0) on empty results; on any other thrown Error or any non-Error throw, coerce to string, write `error.message` (or coerced message) to stderr and `process.exit(1)`. End with `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` — no unconditional `main()` call. Import SkyscannerClient from `./skyscanner/client` (not `./skyscanner-client`). No shebang, no chmod+x, no new runtime deps. ACs here are authoritative for the implementation; verify Price column string assertions against the SKY-003a-test-2 file before declaring done.
acceptanceCriteria: src/cli.ts exists and exports exactly three named symbols with the following signatures: export function parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments, export function validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments, and export async function main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>. No default export and no other runtime exports are introduced.
The types ParsedArguments and ValidatedArguments are defined in cli.ts itself (as exported interfaces or type aliases in the same file). No separate ./arguments module is required or expected.

main() constructs the client as new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey }) (imported from ./skyscanner/client, NOT ./skyscanner-client) and forwards exactly { origin, destination, date, adults } from the validated arguments to searchFlights.
main() MUST await the Promise returned by searchFlights before processing the result; the resolved value is treated as FlightResult[] (an array).
renderTable is imported via import { renderTable } from './table' and renders columns in the fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops.

On an empty searchFlights result set (resolved array of length 0), main() writes the exact string No flights found. to stdout — followed by a single trailing newline produced by the standard output mechanism (e.g., console.log('No flights found.') yields No flights found.\n) — and returns normally with exit code 0, without writing to stderr. A searchFlights rejection or non-array resolution is NOT handled as 'empty'; it is handled per AC-7.

On any thrown Error whose message matches the exact pattern ^exit:[0-9]+$ (where the numeric suffix N is a non-negative integer), main() catches it and calls process.exit(N); this sentinel path MUST NOT write to stderr. A thrown Error whose message does NOT match ^exit:[0-9]+$ (e.g., exit:abc, exit:-1, exit:1.5, exit:, or any unrelated message) is treated as the generic error path: write the error's message to stderr and call process.exit(1). Non-Error throws (strings, numbers, plain objects) MUST be coerced to a string and treated as the generic error path (exit 1, stderr message).

The file terminates with the guard if (require.main === module) { main(); } and contains NO unconditional top-level main() call (no top-level main(); outside the guard, no main().catch(...) at module scope). main() is the sole owner of process.exit invocations and process.stderr writes per the parent story AC-5.
No new runtime dependencies are added to package.json. The file contains no shebang line and no chmod +x directive; CLI invocation remains node dist/cli.js.

stories.title: Write unit tests for Skyscanner API client (client.test.ts)
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.test.ts with at least 8 vitest tests covering the SkyscannerClient, including the two new tests (g) and (h) added to verify the SKY-002 impl story's AC-9 (constructor precedence: apiKey param wins over RAPIDAPI_KEY env var) and AC-10 (invalid apiKey format rejection at the constructor) contracts. All fetch mocking must use vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) with afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); }) and no global beforeAll fetch stub that could leak across tests. Every fetch stub must include headers: { get: () => null }. Success-path stubs must return a plain array from json(). Any test that mutates process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY must restore it in afterEach. vitest run must exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: client.test.ts uses vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) for all fetch mocking — vi.spyOn is not used for fetch
afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); }) is present and restores fetch after every test
Every vi.stubGlobal fetch mock returns an object with: ok (boolean), status (number), json (async function returning data), and headers: { get: () => null }
Success-path fetch stubs return a plain array (not a wrapped object) from json(), matching the client's Array.isArray check
Test (a): verifies correct RapidAPI URL construction from SearchParams and that request headers contain the API key and User-Agent
Test (b): verifies a successful plain-array response body is parsed and returned as FlightResult[]
Test (c): verifies a fetch response with ok=false and a 4xx status causes searchFlights to reject with an Error whose message contains the status code
Test (d): verifies constructing SkyscannerClient with no apiKey and no RAPIDAPI_KEY env var throws an Error referencing the missing key
Test (e): verifies a fetch response whose json() resolves to a non-array or object missing required fields causes searchFlights to reject with a parse/validation Error

Test (f): verifies that when the fetch stub rejects entirely (e.g., vi.stubGlobal('fetch', async () => { throw new Error('network down') })), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i
Any test that sets process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY stores the original value before mutation and restores it (or deletes the key) in afterEach or afterAll
All SkyscannerClient instantiations in tests use the object constructor form: new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: 'valid_api_key' })
The test API key used is 'valid_api_key' or another value matching /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ that contains underscores or hyphens to exercise the correct sanitization regex
vitest run exits 0 with all tests passing and no skipped tests

Test (g): verifies that when both the apiKey constructor parameter (e.g., 'valid_api_key') and process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY (set to a different value) are present, the apiKey constructor parameter takes precedence — the outgoing fetch URL and headers must contain the apiKey parameter value and must NOT contain the env var value, and the env var is restored (or deleted) in afterEach (covers SKY-002 AC-9 constructor-precedence contract)

Test (h): verifies that constructing SkyscannerClient with an apiKey value that fails the /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ sanitization regex (e.g., 'has space', 'has!bang', 'pünctuation', or empty string '') throws an Error whose message references the invalid key or its format, so the constructor rejects bad keys before any fetch is attempted (covers SKY-002 AC-10 invalid-format contract)

client.test.ts does not register a vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) inside beforeAll that would leak across tests; every test installs its own vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) so a per-test stub is never silently shadowed or double-stacked by a leftover global stub from a prior test, and afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals() }) cleanly tears down only what that test installed (prevents double-stub pollution)

stories.title: Implement src/cli.ts entry point implementation
stories.description: Implement `src/cli.ts` as the sole owner of process-exit and stderr responsibilities per parent AC-5. Exports exactly: `parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments`, `validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments`, and `async main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>`. `main()` MUST catch any `Error` whose `message` matches `^exit:[0-9]+$` and call `process.exit(N)`; construct `new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey })`; call `searchFlights({ origin, destination, date, adults })`; render via `renderTable` imported from `./table`; print `No flights found.` (single trailing newline) and return (exit 0) on empty results; on any other thrown Error or any non-Error throw, coerce to string, write `error.message` (or coerced message) to stderr and `process.exit(1)`. End with `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` — no unconditional `main()` call. Import SkyscannerClient from `./skyscanner/client` (not `./skyscanner-client`). No shebang, no chmod+x, no new runtime deps.
acceptanceCriteria: src/cli.ts exists and exports exactly three named symbols with the following signatures: export function parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments, export function validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments, and export async function main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>. No default export and no other runtime exports are introduced.
The types ParsedArguments and ValidatedArguments are defined in cli.ts itself (as exported interfaces or type aliases in the same file). No separate ./arguments module is required or expected.

main() constructs the client as new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey }) (imported from ./skyscanner/client, NOT ./skyscanner-client) and forwards exactly { origin, destination, date, adults } from the validated arguments to searchFlights.
main() MUST await the Promise returned by searchFlights before processing the result; the resolved value is treated as FlightResult[] (an array).
renderTable is imported via import { renderTable } from './table' and renders columns in the fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops.

On an empty searchFlights result set (resolved array of length 0), main() writes the exact string No flights found. to stdout — followed by a single trailing newline produced by the standard output mechanism (e.g., console.log('No flights found.') yields No flights found.\n) — and returns normally with exit code 0, without writing to stderr. A searchFlights rejection or non-array resolution is NOT handled as 'empty'; it is handled per AC-7.

On any thrown Error whose message matches the exact pattern ^exit:[0-9]+$ (where the numeric suffix N is a non-negative integer), main() catches it and calls process.exit(N); this sentinel path MUST NOT write to stderr. A thrown Error whose message does NOT match ^exit:[0-9]+$ (e.g., exit:abc, exit:-1, exit:1.5, exit:, or any unrelated message) is treated as the generic error path: write the error's message to stderr and call process.exit(1). Non-Error throws (strings, numbers, plain objects) MUST be coerced to a string and treated as the generic error path (exit 1, stderr message).

The file terminates with the guard if (require.main === module) { main(); } and contains NO unconditional top-level main() call (no top-level main(); outside the guard, no main().catch(...) at module scope). main() is the sole owner of process.exit invocations and process.stderr writes per the parent story AC-5.

No new runtime dependencies are added to package.json. The file contains no shebang line and no chmod +x directive; CLI invocation remains node dist/cli.js. cli.test.ts is NOT created or modified by this story (owned by SKY-003a).

The main() function MUST handle sentinel errors that match /^exit:[0-9]+$/ by calling process.exit(N) without writing to stderr, and generic Errors by writing their message to stderr and calling process.exit(1); non-Error throws are coerced to strings and treated as generic errors (stderr + exit 1).

Exports exactly: `parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments`, `validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments`, and `async main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>`. `main()` MUST catch any `Error` whose `message` matches `^exit:[0-9]+$` and call `process.exit(N)`; construct `new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey })`; call `searchFlights({ origin, destination, date, adults })`; render via `renderTable` imported from `./table`; print `No flights found.` (single trailing newline) and return (exit 0) on empty results; on any other thrown Error or any non-Error throw, coerce to string, write `error.message` (or coerced message) to stderr and `process.exit(1)`. End with `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` — no unconditional `main()` call. Import SkyscannerClient from `./skyscanner/client` (not `./skyscanner-client`). No shebang, no chmod+x, no new runtime deps. ACs here are authoritative for the implementation; verify Price column string assertions against the SKY-003a-test-2 file before declaring done.
acceptanceCriteria: src/cli.ts exists and exports exactly three named symbols with the following signatures: export function parseArguments(argv: string[]): ParsedArguments, export function validateArguments(parsed: ParsedArguments, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): ValidatedArguments, and export async function main(argv?: string[], env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<void>. No default export and no other runtime exports are introduced.
The types ParsedArguments and ValidatedArguments are defined in cli.ts itself (as exported interfaces or type aliases in the same file). No separate ./arguments module is required or expected.

main() constructs the client as new SkyscannerClient({ apiKey: validated.rapidApiKey }) (imported from ./skyscanner/client, NOT ./skyscanner-client) and forwards exactly { origin, destination, date, adults } from the validated arguments to searchFlights.
main() MUST await the Promise returned by searchFlights before processing the result; the resolved value is treated as FlightResult[] (an array).
renderTable is imported via import { renderTable } from './table' and renders columns in the fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops.

On an empty searchFlights result set (resolved array of length 0), main() writes the exact string No flights found. to stdout — followed by a single trailing newline produced by the standard output mechanism (e.g., console.log('No flights found.') yields No flights found.\n) — and returns normally with exit code 0, without writing to stderr. A searchFlights rejection or non-array resolution is NOT handled as 'empty'; it is handled per AC-7.

On any thrown Error whose message matches the exact pattern ^exit:[0-9]+$ (where the numeric suffix N is a non-negative integer), main() catches it and calls process.exit(N); this sentinel path MUST NOT write to stderr. A thrown Error whose message does NOT match ^exit:[0-9]+$ (e.g., exit:abc, exit:-1, exit:1.5, exit:, or any unrelated message) is treated as the generic error path: write the error's message to stderr and call process.exit(1). Non-Error throws (strings, numbers, plain objects) MUST be coerced to a string and treated as the generic error path (exit 1, stderr message).

The file terminates with the guard if (require.main === module) { main(); } and contains NO unconditional top-level main() call (no top-level main(); outside the guard, no main().catch(...) at module scope). main() is the sole owner of process.exit invocations and process.stderr writes per the parent story AC-5.

stories.title: Add comprehensive unit tests for cli.ts with test isolation and contract verification
stories.description: Create comprehensive unit tests for cli.ts covering all code paths with proper test isolation and contract verification.
acceptanceCriteria: src/cli.test.ts exists at /tmp/skyscanner-app/src/cli.test.ts and is the sole test file for src/cli.ts; no other file under src/ defines tests for cli.ts exports.

parseArguments is covered by tests asserting: default origin/destination/date/adults when no flags are provided, correct override values when --origin/--destination/--date/--adults flags are supplied, and a thrown or rejected error for malformed input (e.g. invalid date or non-numeric --adults).

validateArguments is covered by tests asserting: returns the validated object (including rapidApiKey) when RAPIDAPI_KEY is present in env, throws when RAPIDAPI_KEY is missing, and throws when RAPIDAPI_KEY is an empty string.
validateArguments properly rejects null or undefined values for required environment variables.

main() happy path is covered by a test that stubs the network/API layer so no real HTTP request is made, invokes main() with explicit argv and env, and asserts: stdout contains the rendered table output, stderr is empty, and the resolved/process exit code is 0 (or process.exit is called with 0 via the Error('exit:N') sentinel).
main() empty-results path is covered by a test that stubs the client to resolve an empty flight list and asserts: stdout equals exactly 'No flights found.', stderr is empty, and exit code is 0.

main() error and Error('exit:N') sentinel paths are covered by tests asserting: (a) when a non-sentinel error is thrown, the message appears on stderr, stdout is empty, and exit code is 1; (b) when Error('exit:N') is thrown, process.exit is called with N and no unhandled rejection escapes main().

All tests in src/cli.test.ts pass when executed via the project's configured test command (from SKY-001); the test run performs zero network I/O (asserted by stubbing/spying the network boundary, e.g. SkyscannerClient or the underlying fetch/http call).
Test isolation AC is implemented: vi.clearAllMocks is called in beforeEach, and all spies are restored in afterEach to prevent state leakage between test cases.
Data-flow-contract test verifies that searchFlights is called with {origin, destination, date, adults} exactly — no extra, missing, or altered properties.

Non-Error throw test: throwing a string (e.g. 'invalid key') or object (e.g. {code: 500}) does not crash the process; instead, the error message is written to stderr, stdout is empty, and exit code is 1.

Human-readable message requirement: When parseArguments rejects invalid date input, the error message must contain the word `date` and the offending value (e.g., 'Invalid date: abc'); when rejecting non-numeric adults, the message must contain the word `adults` and the value (e.g., 'Invalid adults: xyz').

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client (client.ts) - Response Handling and Pagination
stories.description: Handle API response validation, pagination, and error conditions for Skyscanner API client
acceptanceCriteria: When the response body is not a plain array, or is missing any of the seven required FlightResult fields (price, currency, airline, departure, arrival, duration, stops) on any element, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error
searchFlights checks res.headers?.get?.('x-next-page') for pagination and fetches subsequent pages if the header is present and non-null, concatenating results before resolving
When fetch itself rejects (network-level failure), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i
When adults is omitted from SearchParams, the URL does not contain 'undefined' as a query parameter value
tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no type errors
When searchFlights is called with non-numeric adults, the URL does not contain 'NaN' as a query parameter value
When searchFlights is called with a malformed date (e.g., 'invalid-date'), the error message specifies that date validation failed
When the API returns an empty array of flights, searchFlights resolves with an empty array

When a subsequent pagination request fails with a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the numeric HTTP status code of the failed page, not the original request

When searchFlights is called with an API key that is a number, the constructor throws an Error

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client - Error Handling and Response Processing
stories.description: Implement HTTP error handling, malformed-response detection and pagination
acceptanceCriteria: When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the numeric HTTP status code but not the apiKey value and not the full request URL

When the response body is not a plain array, or is missing any of the seven required FlightResult fields (price, currency, airline, departure, arrival, duration, stops) on any element, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error
searchFlights checks res.headers?.get?.('x-next-page') for pagination and fetches subsequent pages if the header is present and non-null, concatenating results before resolving
When the API returns an empty array of flights, searchFlights resolves with an empty array
When the API returns a response with a non-string x-next-page header value, searchFlights does not attempt to fetch additional pages
When a subsequent pagination request fails with a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the numeric HTTP status code of the failed page, not the original request
When the API returns a malformed response for pagination continuation, searchFlights does not attempt to fetch additional pages
When fetch itself rejects (network-level failure), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i
When fetch returns a non-JSON response body, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse error
When the API returns a response with a missing airline name, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns a response with a missing departure time, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns a response with a missing arrival time, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns a response with a missing currency value, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns a response with a numeric value for any flight field that should be a string, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns a response that includes flight data with an invalid field, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive validation error
When the API returns an error response with a status code in the 400 range, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the status code
When the API returns an error response with a status code in the 500 range, searchFlights rejects with an Error containing the status code
